# gh-1604: Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone

## Description

## Problem
On long-horizon tasks the model-visible stream accretes without bound: (a) the background-jobs wall re-renders the full shell-job registry — every historical job card with its full command label — after assistant messages, so by job ~60 each turn carries thousands of duplicated tokens forever; (b) no auto-compaction kicks in during 30-min sessions even as the context passes 100K+; (c) single tool results (full-file dumps, 62K-line disassemblies) enter the context unsanitized. Input tokens (mostly cache reads) explode: run 7 totaled 60.3M input tokens for 30 trials.

## Evidence
- `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-7/result.json`: `"n_input_tokens": 60294423, "n_cache_tokens": 57303872` for 30 trials.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/result.json`: 11,170,936 input tokens in one 1800s trial; siblings ZrXediE 8.16M, GacsJot 7.56M; make-doom-for-mips kveR2Mi 6.41M, 9na3H9U 4.23M, cawBRSD 4.15M — the two MIPS tasks account for ~46M of run 7's 60.3M.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/agent/fah-sessions/--app--/*.jsonl`: consecutive `shell_job_registry` custom records re-emitted after nearly every assistant message, each listing ALL jobs (60+ entries) with complete command strings (~10KB per record), e.g. entries sh-11…sh-60 all present in one snapshot.
- `make-doom-for-mips__cawBRSD/agent/fa.txt`: repeated whole-file dumps (`cat .../doomgeneric_img.c; ...; sed -n 1690,1968p /app/vm.js`) with no summarization pressure.
- Upstream has related issues (#429 transcript wall, #1073 JSONL disk growth) — this issue covers the model-context/token cost on benches, not disk or UI.

## Proposed fix
- Truncate job cards in the model-visible registry: keep id, state, exit code, first/last ~120 chars of the command; drop stale done/lost cards from the rendered wall after they've been acknowledged (render only running + last K completed).
- Supersede/compact registry snapshots in context instead of re-sending the full history each turn.
- Bench-profile auto-compaction: trigger summarization when context exceeds a token threshold (e.g., 60-80K) or after N minutes, keeping the task text + a rolling summary; make the threshold configurable via env for bench runs.
- Cap single tool outputs at M chars with a `… N chars truncated` marker plus an offset-follow-up affordance.

## Acceptance
1. Deterministic fixture reproducing a 60-job session: total context tokens for the registry shrink by ≥10x; the wall never exceeds K lines.
2. Replay of the jF7GNFh turn profile with the new caps: projected total input tokens ≤ ~3M (vs 11.2M).
3. Compaction events are visible in the session JSONL and preserve task text, ledger obligations, and the latest tool results.

Shared by the `bash_job` status wall and the job-settle system notice (was: full command in both). - `withCompactionTriggerTokens` raises the compaction reserve so `shouldCompact` fires at the trigger; guards: keep-recent ≤ trigger/2 (a pass always frees), trigger ≥ default threshold is a no-op, junk env is ignored (byte-identical legacy). # gh-1604: Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone

## Description

## Problem
On long-horizon tasks the model-visible stream accretes without bound: (a) the background-jobs wall re-renders the full shell-job registry — every historical job card with its full command label — after assistant messages, so by job ~60 each turn carries thousands of duplicated tokens forever; (b) no auto-compaction kicks in during 30-min sessions even as the context passes 100K+; (c) single tool results (full-file dumps, 62K-line disassemblies) enter the context unsanitized. Input tokens (mostly cache reads) explode: run 7 totaled 60.3M input tokens for 30 trials.

## Evidence
- `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-7/result.json`: `"n_input_tokens": 60294423, "n_cache_tokens": 57303872` for 30 trials.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/result.json`: 11,170,936 input tokens in one 1800s trial; siblings ZrXediE 8.16M, GacsJot 7.56M; make-doom-for-mips kveR2Mi 6.41M, 9na3H9U 4.23M, cawBRSD 4.15M — the two MIPS tasks account for ~46M of run 7's 60.3M.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/agent/fah-sessions/--app--/*.jsonl`: consecutive `shell_job_registry` custom records re-emitted after nearly every assistant message, each listing ALL jobs (60+ entries) with complete command strings (~10KB per record), e.g. entries sh-11…sh-60 all present in one snapshot.
- `make-doom-for-mips__cawBRSD/agent/fa.txt`: repeated whole-file dumps (`cat .../doomgeneric_img.c; ...; sed -n 1690,1968p /app/vm.js`) with no summarization pressure.
- Upstream has related issues (#429 transcript wall, #1073 JSONL disk growth) — this issue covers the model-context/token cost on benches, not disk or UI.

## Proposed fix
- Truncate job cards in the model-visible registry: keep id, state, exit code, first/last ~120 chars of the command; drop stale done/lost cards from the rendered wall after they've been acknowledged (render only running + last K completed).
- Supersede/compact registry snapshots in context instead of re-sending the full history each turn.
- Bench-profile auto-compaction: trigger summarization when context exceeds a token threshold (e.g., 60-80K) or after N minutes, keeping the task text + a rolling summary; make the threshold configurable via env for bench runs.
- Cap single tool outputs at M chars with a `… N chars truncated` marker plus an offset-follow-up affordance.

## Acceptance
1. Deterministic fixture reproducing a 60-job session: total context tokens for the registry shrink by ≥10x; the wall never exceeds K lines.
2. Replay of the jF7GNFh turn profile with the new caps: projected total input tokens ≤ ~3M (vs 11.2M).
3. Compaction events are visible in the session JSONL and preserve task text, ledger obligations, and the latest tool results.

## Machine jobs

# gh-1604: Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone

## Description

## Problem
On long-horizon tasks the model-visible stream accretes without bound: (a) the background-jobs wall re-renders the full shell-job registry — every historical job card with its full command label — after assistant messages, so by job ~60 each turn carries thousands of duplicated tokens forever; (b) no auto-compaction kicks in during 30-min sessions even as the context passes 100K+; (c) single tool results (full-file dumps, 62K-line disassemblies) enter the context unsanitized. Input tokens (mostly cache reads) explode: run 7 totaled 60.3M input tokens for 30 trials.

## Evidence
- `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-7/result.json`: `"n_input_tokens": 60294423, "n_cache_tokens": 57303872` for 30 trials.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/result.json`: 11,170,936 input tokens in one 1800s trial; siblings ZrXediE 8.16M, GacsJot 7.56M; make-doom-for-mips kveR2Mi 6.41M, 9na3H9U 4.23M, cawBRSD 4.15M — the two MIPS tasks account for ~46M of run 7's 60.3M.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/agent/fah-sessions/--app--/*.jsonl`: consecutive `shell_job_registry` custom records re-emitted after nearly every assistant message, each listing ALL jobs (60+ entries) with complete command strings (~10KB per record), e.g. entries sh-11…sh-60 all present in one snapshot.
- `make-doom-for-mips__cawBRSD/agent/fa.txt`: repeated whole-file dumps (`cat .../doomgeneric_img.c; ...; sed -n 1690,1968p /app/vm.js`) with no summarization pressure.
- Upstream has related issues (#429 transcript wall, #1073 JSONL disk growth) — this issue covers the model-context/token cost on benches, not disk or UI.

## Proposed fix
- Truncate job cards in the model-visible registry: keep id, state, exit code, first/last ~120 chars of the command; drop stale done/lost cards from the rendered wall after they've been acknowledged (render only running + last K completed).
- Supersede/compact registry snapshots in context instead of re-sending the full history each turn.
- Bench-profile auto-compaction: trigger summarization when context exceeds a token threshold (e.g., 60-80K) or after N minutes, keeping the task text + a rolling summary; make the threshold configurable via env for bench runs.
- Cap single tool outputs at M chars with a `… N chars truncated` marker plus an offset-follow-up affordance.

## Acceptance
1. Deterministic fixture reproducing a 60-job session: total context tokens for the registry shrink by ≥10x; the wall never exceeds K lines.
2. Replay of the jF7GNFh turn profile with the new caps: projected total input tokens ≤ ~3M (vs 11.2M).
3. Compaction events are visible in the session JSONL and preserve task text, ledger obligations, and the latest tool results.

## Machine jobs

# gh-1604: Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone

## Description

## Problem
On long-horizon tasks the model-visible stream accretes without bound: (a) the background-jobs wall re-renders the full shell-job registry — every historical job card with its full command label — after assistant messages, so by job ~60 each turn carries thousands of duplicated tokens forever; (b) no auto-compaction kicks in during 30-min sessions even as the context passes 100K+; (c) single tool results (full-file dumps, 62K-line disassemblies) enter the context unsanitized. Input tokens (mostly cache reads) explode: run 7 totaled 60.3M input tokens for 30 trials.

## Evidence
- `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-7/result.json`: `"n_input_tokens": 60294423, "n_cache_tokens": 57303872` for 30 trials.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/result.json`: 11,170,936 input tokens in one 1800s trial; siblings ZrXediE 8.16M, GacsJot 7.56M; make-doom-for-mips kveR2Mi 6.41M, 9na3H9U 4.23M, cawBRSD 4.15M — the two MIPS tasks account for ~46M of run 7's 60.3M.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/agent/fah-sessions/--app--/*.jsonl`: consecutive `shell_job_registry` custom records re-emitted after nearly every assistant message, each listing ALL jobs (60+ entries) with complete command strings (~10KB per record), e.g. entries sh-11…sh-60 all present in one snapshot.
- `make-doom-for-mips__cawBRSD/agent/fa.txt`: repeated whole-file dumps (`cat .../doomgeneric_img.c; ...; sed -n 1690,1968p /app/vm.js`) with no summarization pressure.
- Upstream has related issues (#429 transcript wall, #1073 JSONL disk growth) — this issue covers the model-context/token cost on benches, not disk or UI.

## Proposed fix
- Truncate job cards in the model-visible registry: keep id, state, exit code, first/last ~120 chars of the command; drop stale done/lost cards from the rendered wall after they've been acknowledged (render only running + last K completed).
- Supersede/compact registry snapshots in context instead of re-sending the full history each turn.
- Bench-profile auto-compaction: trigger summarization when context exceeds a token threshold (e.g., 60-80K) or after N minutes, keeping the task text + a rolling summary; make the threshold configurable via env for bench runs.
- Cap single tool outputs at M chars with a `… N chars truncated` marker plus an offset-follow-up affordance.

## Acceptance
1. Deterministic fixture reproducing a 60-job session: total context tokens for the registry shrink by ≥10x; the wall never exceeds K lines.
2. Replay of the jF7GNFh turn profile with the new caps: projected total input tokens ≤ ~3M (vs 11.2M).
3. Compaction events are visible in the session JSONL and preserve task text, ledger obligations, and the latest tool results.

# gh-1604: Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone

## Description

## Problem
On long-horizon tasks the model-visible stream accretes without bound: (a) the background-jobs wall re-renders the full shell-job registry — every historical job card with its full command label — after assistant messages, so by job ~60 each turn carries thousands of duplicated tokens forever; (b) no auto-compaction kicks in during 30-min sessions even as the context passes 100K+; (c) single tool results (full-file dumps, 62K-line disassemblies) enter the context unsanitized. Input tokens (mostly cache reads) explode: run 7 totaled 60.3M input tokens for 30 trials.

## Evidence
- `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-7/result.json`: `"n_input_tokens": 60294423, "n_cache_tokens": 57303872` for 30 trials.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/result.json`: 11,170,936 input tokens in one 1800s trial; siblings ZrXediE 8.16M, GacsJot 7.56M; make-doom-for-mips kveR2Mi 6.41M, 9na3H9U 4.23M, cawBRSD 4.15M — the two MIPS tasks account for ~46M of run 7's 60.3M.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/agent/fah-sessions/--app--/*.jsonl`: consecutive `shell_job_registry` custom records re-emitted after nearly every assistant message, each listing ALL jobs (60+ entries) with complete command strings (~10KB per record), e.g. entries sh-11…sh-60 all present in one snapshot.
- `make-doom-for-mips__cawBRSD/agent/fa.txt`: repeated whole-file dumps (`cat .../doomgeneric_img.c; ...; sed -n 1690,1968p /app/vm.js`) with no summarization pressure.
- Upstream has related issues (#429 transcript wall, #1073 JSONL disk growth) — this issue covers the model-context/token cost on benches, not disk or UI.

## Proposed fix
- Truncate job cards in the model-visible registry: keep id, state, exit code, first/last ~120 chars of the command; drop stale done/lost cards from the rendered wall after they've been acknowledged (render only running + last K completed).
- Supersede/compact registry snapshots in context instead of re-sending the full history each turn.
- Bench-profile auto-compaction: trigger summarization when context exceeds a token threshold (e.g., 60-80K) or after N minutes, keeping the task text + a rolling summary; make the threshold configurable via env for bench runs.
- Cap single tool outputs at M chars with a `… N chars truncated` marker plus an offset-follow-up affordance.

## Acceptance
1. Deterministic fixture reproducing a 60-job session: total context tokens for the registry shrink by ≥10x; the wall never exceeds K lines.
2. Replay of the jF7GNFh turn profile with the new caps: projected total input tokens ≤ ~3M (vs 11.2M).
3. Compaction events are visible in the session JSONL and preserve task text, ledger obligations, and the latest tool results.

# gh-1604: Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone

## Description

## Problem
On long-horizon tasks the model-visible stream accretes without bound: (a) the background-jobs wall re-renders the full shell-job registry — every historical job card with its full command label — after assistant messages, so by job ~60 each turn carries thousands of duplicated tokens forever; (b) no auto-compaction kicks in during 30-min sessions even as the context passes 100K+; (c) single tool results (full-file dumps, 62K-line disassemblies) enter the context unsanitized. Input tokens (mostly cache reads) explode: run 7 totaled 60.3M input tokens for 30 trials.

## Evidence
- `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-7/result.json`: `"n_input_tokens": 60294423, "n_cache_tokens": 57303872` for 30 trials.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/result.json`: 11,170,936 input tokens in one 1800s trial; siblings ZrXediE 8.16M, GacsJot 7.56M; make-doom-for-mips kveR2Mi 6.41M, 9na3H9U 4.23M, cawBRSD 4.15M — the two MIPS tasks account for ~46M of run 7's 60.3M.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/agent/fah-sessions/--app--/*.jsonl`: consecutive `shell_job_registry` custom records re-emitted after nearly every assistant message, each listing ALL jobs (60+ entries) with complete command strings (~10KB per record), e.g. entries sh-11…sh-60 all present in one snapshot.
- `make-doom-for-mips__cawBRSD/agent/fa.txt`: repeated whole-file dumps (`cat .../doomgeneric_img.c; ...; sed -n 1690,1968p /app/vm.js`) with no summarization pressure.
- Upstream has related issues (#429 transcript wall, #1073 JSONL disk growth) — this issue covers the model-context/token cost on benches, not disk or UI.

## Proposed fix
- Truncate job cards in the model-visible registry: keep id, state, exit code, first/last ~120 chars of the command; drop stale done/lost cards from the rendered wall after they've been acknowledged (render only running + last K completed).
- Supersede/compact registry snapshots in context instead of re-sending the full history each turn.
- Bench-profile auto-compaction: trigger summarization when context exceeds a token threshold (e.g., 60-80K) or after N minutes, keeping the task text + a rolling summary; make the threshold configurable via env for bench runs.
- Cap single tool outputs at M chars with a `… N chars truncated` marker plus an offset-follow-up affordance.

## Acceptance
1. Deterministic fixture reproducing a 60-job session: total context tokens for the registry shrink by ≥10x; the wall never exceeds K lines.
2. Replay of the jF7GNFh turn profile with the new caps: projected total input tokens ≤ ~3M (vs 11.2M).
3. Compaction events are visible in the session JSONL and preserve task text, ledger obligations, and the latest tool results.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1612 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1612 - **Title**: gh-1604 Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1604` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 12 - **Additions**: +1118 - **Deletions**: -23 - **Created**: 2026-10-14T14:50:41Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-14T15:29:57Z ## PR Description Closes #1604 ### What changed Bounds the model-visible cost of long bench runs (gh-1604): background-job commands are truncated to a bounded label on every model-facing surface, a bench env knob (`FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS`) lowers the auto-compaction trigger to an absolute context size so long trials compact mid-run instead of accreting, and a `FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD` env knob enables the tool-output spill cap per run without a config file. ### Key decisions - New `shellJobCommandLabel` (pure, surrogate-safe): single-line commands keep the first/last 120 chars of the whitespace-flattened command with a `[…N chars…]` marker naming the true omitted size; multi-line commands keep the bounded FIRST LINE only (issue #599 RED contract — a heredoc body is never a transcript row source, and a flattened head or whole-command tail would echo body lines back through every settle notice). Shared by the `bash_job` status wall and the job-settle system notice (was: full command in both). - `withCompactionTriggerTokens` raises the compaction reserve so `shouldCompact` fires at the trigger; guards: keep-recent ≤ trigger/2 (a pass always frees), trigger ≥ default threshold is a no-op, junk env is ignored (byte-identical legacy). Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override. - Task preservation rides the existing mechanisms, verified end-to-end: the checkpoint summarizer prompt carries the task text; the obligations-ledger block and the latest tool result (protected tail) survive in the post-compaction projection; the checkpoint record is visible in the session JSONL. - `resolveRunSpillsConfig` composes the env knob over the yaml section (env wins; `0` disables); `buildPreview` no longer duplicates a body smaller than its head+tail bounds. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/tools/shell_job_command_label_test.dart \ test/compaction/bench_trigger_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart \ test/spill/spill_env_test.dart ``` `agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` is the end-to-end proof: with the env set the compaction fires mid-run where the default (183k-token trigger) never would, every later turn request stays under the bench trigger, and the control run (no env) compacts nothing at the same sizes. ### Coverage notes - AC1 is covered by the deterministic fixture in `shell_job_command_label_test.dart`: a 60-job registry renders ≥10x less model-visible material than the pre-fix shape, and the status wall stays within K lines (running + last 20 exited + overflow tail). - AC2's full turn-profile replay was not built; the per-request bound is asserted directly instead (every post-crossing turn request ≤ the trigger). - AC3 is covered by the CLI test (JSONL event, task text in the summarizer request, ledger + latest tool result in the projection).
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD ENV["bench env knobs"] --> BT["resolveBenchCompactionSettings"] BT --> GATE["shouldCompact fires at the trigger"] GATE --> ENG["structured compaction (existing)"] ENG --> CKPT["CompactCheckpointRecord in JSONL
(task text → summarizer prompt;
ledger + latest tool results → protected tail)"] JOBS["bash background jobs"] --> LBL["shellJobCommandLabel"] LBL --> WALL["bash_job status wall + settle notice"] SPILL["FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD"] --> RC["resolveRunSpillsConfig"] RC --> HOOKS["spill hooks (existing)"] ```

# gh-1604: Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone

## Description

## Problem
On long-horizon tasks the model-visible stream accretes without bound: (a) the background-jobs wall re-renders the full shell-job registry — every historical job card with its full command label — after assistant messages, so by job ~60 each turn carries thousands of duplicated tokens forever; (b) no auto-compaction kicks in during 30-min sessions even as the context passes 100K+; (c) single tool results (full-file dumps, 62K-line disassemblies) enter the context unsanitized. Input tokens (mostly cache reads) explode: run 7 totaled 60.3M input tokens for 30 trials.

## Evidence
- `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-7/result.json`: `"n_input_tokens": 60294423, "n_cache_tokens": 57303872` for 30 trials.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/result.json`: 11,170,936 input tokens in one 1800s trial; siblings ZrXediE 8.16M, GacsJot 7.56M; make-doom-for-mips kveR2Mi 6.41M, 9na3H9U 4.23M, cawBRSD 4.15M — the two MIPS tasks account for ~46M of run 7's 60.3M.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/agent/fah-sessions/--app--/*.jsonl`: consecutive `shell_job_registry` custom records re-emitted after nearly every assistant message, each listing ALL jobs (60+ entries) with complete command strings (~10KB per record), e.g. entries sh-11…sh-60 all present in one snapshot.
- `make-doom-for-mips__cawBRSD/agent/fa.txt`: repeated whole-file dumps (`cat .../doomgeneric_img.c; ...; sed -n 1690,1968p /app/vm.js`) with no summarization pressure.
- Upstream has related issues (#429 transcript wall, #1073 JSONL disk growth) — this issue covers the model-context/token cost on benches, not disk or UI.

## Proposed fix
- Truncate job cards in the model-visible registry: keep id, state, exit code, first/last ~120 chars of the command; drop stale done/lost cards from the rendered wall after they've been acknowledged (render only running + last K completed).
- Supersede/compact registry snapshots in context instead of re-sending the full history each turn.
- Bench-profile auto-compaction: trigger summarization when context exceeds a token threshold (e.g., 60-80K) or after N minutes, keeping the task text + a rolling summary; make the threshold configurable via env for bench runs.
- Cap single tool outputs at M chars with a `… N chars truncated` marker plus an offset-follow-up affordance.

## Acceptance
1. Deterministic fixture reproducing a 60-job session: total context tokens for the registry shrink by ≥10x; the wall never exceeds K lines.
2. Replay of the jF7GNFh turn profile with the new caps: projected total input tokens ≤ ~3M (vs 11.2M).
3. Compaction events are visible in the session JSONL and preserve task text, ledger obligations, and the latest tool results.

Shared by the `bash_job` status wall and the job-settle system notice (was: full command in both). - `withCompactionTriggerTokens` raises the compaction reserve so `shouldCompact` fires at the trigger; guards: keep-recent ≤ trigger/2 (a pass always frees), trigger ≥ default threshold is a no-op, junk env is ignored (byte-identical legacy). Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override. - Task preservation rides the existing mechanisms, verified end-to-end: the checkpoint summarizer prompt carries the task text; the obligations-ledger block and the latest tool result (protected tail) survive in the post-compaction projection; the checkpoint record is visible in the session JSONL. - `resolveRunSpillsConfig` composes the env knob over the yaml section (env wins; `0` disables); `buildPreview` no longer duplicates a body smaller than its head+tail bounds. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/tools/shell_job_command_label_test.dart \ test/compaction/bench_trigger_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart \ test/spill/spill_env_test.dart ``` `agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` is the end-to-end proof: with the env set the compaction fires mid-run where the default (183k-token trigger) never would, every later turn request stays under the bench trigger, and the control run (no env) compacts nothing at the same sizes. ### Coverage notes - AC1 is covered by the deterministic fixture in `shell_job_command_label_test.dart`: a 60-job registry renders ≥10x less model-visible material than the pre-fix shape, and the status wall stays within K lines (running + last 20 exited + overflow tail). - AC2's full turn-profile replay was not built; the per-request bound is asserted directly instead (every post-crossing turn request ≤ the trigger). - AC3 is covered by the CLI test (JSONL event, task text in the summarizer request, ledger + latest tool result in the projection).

# gh-1604: Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone

## Description

## Problem
On long-horizon tasks the model-visible stream accretes without bound: (a) the background-jobs wall re-renders the full shell-job registry — every historical job card with its full command label — after assistant messages, so by job ~60 each turn carries thousands of duplicated tokens forever; (b) no auto-compaction kicks in during 30-min sessions even as the context passes 100K+; (c) single tool results (full-file dumps, 62K-line disassemblies) enter the context unsanitized. Input tokens (mostly cache reads) explode: run 7 totaled 60.3M input tokens for 30 trials.

## Evidence
- `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-7/result.json`: `"n_input_tokens": 60294423, "n_cache_tokens": 57303872` for 30 trials.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/result.json`: 11,170,936 input tokens in one 1800s trial; siblings ZrXediE 8.16M, GacsJot 7.56M; make-doom-for-mips kveR2Mi 6.41M, 9na3H9U 4.23M, cawBRSD 4.15M — the two MIPS tasks account for ~46M of run 7's 60.3M.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/agent/fah-sessions/--app--/*.jsonl`: consecutive `shell_job_registry` custom records re-emitted after nearly every assistant message, each listing ALL jobs (60+ entries) with complete command strings (~10KB per record), e.g. entries sh-11…sh-60 all present in one snapshot.
- `make-doom-for-mips__cawBRSD/agent/fa.txt`: repeated whole-file dumps (`cat .../doomgeneric_img.c; ...; sed -n 1690,1968p /app/vm.js`) with no summarization pressure.
- Upstream has related issues (#429 transcript wall, #1073 JSONL disk growth) — this issue covers the model-context/token cost on benches, not disk or UI.

## Proposed fix
- Truncate job cards in the model-visible registry: keep id, state, exit code, first/last ~120 chars of the command; drop stale done/lost cards from the rendered wall after they've been acknowledged (render only running + last K completed).
- Supersede/compact registry snapshots in context instead of re-sending the full history each turn.
- Bench-profile auto-compaction: trigger summarization when context exceeds a token threshold (e.g., 60-80K) or after N minutes, keeping the task text + a rolling summary; make the threshold configurable via env for bench runs.
- Cap single tool outputs at M chars with a `… N chars truncated` marker plus an offset-follow-up affordance.

## Acceptance
1. Deterministic fixture reproducing a 60-job session: total context tokens for the registry shrink by ≥10x; the wall never exceeds K lines.
2. Replay of the jF7GNFh turn profile with the new caps: projected total input tokens ≤ ~3M (vs 11.2M).
3. Compaction events are visible in the session JSONL and preserve task text, ledger obligations, and the latest tool results.

# gh-1604: Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone

## Description

## Problem
On long-horizon tasks the model-visible stream accretes without bound: (a) the background-jobs wall re-renders the full shell-job registry — every historical job card with its full command label — after assistant messages, so by job ~60 each turn carries thousands of duplicated tokens forever; (b) no auto-compaction kicks in during 30-min sessions even as the context passes 100K+; (c) single tool results (full-file dumps, 62K-line disassemblies) enter the context unsanitized. Input tokens (mostly cache reads) explode: run 7 totaled 60.3M input tokens for 30 trials.

## Evidence
- `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-7/result.json`: `"n_input_tokens": 60294423, "n_cache_tokens": 57303872` for 30 trials.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/result.json`: 11,170,936 input tokens in one 1800s trial; siblings ZrXediE 8.16M, GacsJot 7.56M; make-doom-for-mips kveR2Mi 6.41M, 9na3H9U 4.23M, cawBRSD 4.15M — the two MIPS tasks account for ~46M of run 7's 60.3M.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/agent/fah-sessions/--app--/*.jsonl`: consecutive `shell_job_registry` custom records re-emitted after nearly every assistant message, each listing ALL jobs (60+ entries) with complete command strings (~10KB per record), e.g. entries sh-11…sh-60 all present in one snapshot.
- `make-doom-for-mips__cawBRSD/agent/fa.txt`: repeated whole-file dumps (`cat .../doomgeneric_img.c; ...; sed -n 1690,1968p /app/vm.js`) with no summarization pressure.
- Upstream has related issues (#429 transcript wall, #1073 JSONL disk growth) — this issue covers the model-context/token cost on benches, not disk or UI.

## Proposed fix
- Truncate job cards in the model-visible registry: keep id, state, exit code, first/last ~120 chars of the command; drop stale done/lost cards from the rendered wall after they've been acknowledged (render only running + last K completed).
- Supersede/compact registry snapshots in context instead of re-sending the full history each turn.
- Bench-profile auto-compaction: trigger summarization when context exceeds a token threshold (e.g., 60-80K) or after N minutes, keeping the task text + a rolling summary; make the threshold configurable via env for bench runs.
- Cap single tool outputs at M chars with a `… N chars truncated` marker plus an offset-follow-up affordance.

## Acceptance
1. Deterministic fixture reproducing a 60-job session: total context tokens for the registry shrink by ≥10x; the wall never exceeds K lines.
2. Replay of the jF7GNFh turn profile with the new caps: projected total input tokens ≤ ~3M (vs 11.2M).
3. Compaction events are visible in the session JSONL and preserve task text, ledger obligations, and the latest tool results.

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1612 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1612 - **Title**: gh-1604 Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1604` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 12 - **Additions**: +1118 - **Deletions**: -23 - **Created**: 2026-10-14T14:50:41Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-14T15:29:57Z ## PR Description Closes #1604 ### What changed Bounds the model-visible cost of long bench runs (gh-1604): background-job commands are truncated to a bounded label on every model-facing surface, a bench env knob (`FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS`) lowers the auto-compaction trigger to an absolute context size so long trials compact mid-run instead of accreting, and a `FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD` env knob enables the tool-output spill cap per run without a config file. ### Key decisions - New `shellJobCommandLabel` (pure, surrogate-safe): single-line commands keep the first/last 120 chars of the whitespace-flattened command with a `[…N chars…]` marker naming the true omitted size; multi-line commands keep the bounded FIRST LINE only (issue #599 RED contract — a heredoc body is never a transcript row source, and a flattened head or whole-command tail would echo body lines back through every settle notice). Shared by the `bash_job` status wall and the job-settle system notice (was: full command in both). - `withCompactionTriggerTokens` raises the compaction reserve so `shouldCompact` fires at the trigger; guards: keep-recent ≤ trigger/2 (a pass always frees), trigger ≥ default threshold is a no-op, junk env is ignored (byte-identical legacy). Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override. - Task preservation rides the existing mechanisms, verified end-to-end: the checkpoint summarizer prompt carries the task text; the obligations-ledger block and the latest tool result (protected tail) survive in the post-compaction projection; the checkpoint record is visible in the session JSONL. - `resolveRunSpillsConfig` composes the env knob over the yaml section (env wins; `0` disables); `buildPreview` no longer duplicates a body smaller than its head+tail bounds. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/tools/shell_job_command_label_test.dart \ test/compaction/bench_trigger_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart \ test/spill/spill_env_test.dart ``` `agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` is the end-to-end proof: with the env set the compaction fires mid-run where the default (183k-token trigger) never would, every later turn request stays under the bench trigger, and the control run (no env) compacts nothing at the same sizes. ### Coverage notes - AC1 is covered by the deterministic fixture in `shell_job_command_label_test.dart`: a 60-job registry renders ≥10x less model-visible material than the pre-fix shape, and the status wall stays within K lines (running + last 20 exited + overflow tail). - AC2's full turn-profile replay was not built; the per-request bound is asserted directly instead (every post-crossing turn request ≤ the trigger). - AC3 is covered by the CLI test (JSONL event, task text in the summarizer request, ledger + latest tool result in the projection).

# gh-1604: Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone

## Description

## Problem
On long-horizon tasks the model-visible stream accretes without bound: (a) the background-jobs wall re-renders the full shell-job registry — every historical job card with its full command label — after assistant messages, so by job ~60 each turn carries thousands of duplicated tokens forever; (b) no auto-compaction kicks in during 30-min sessions even as the context passes 100K+; (c) single tool results (full-file dumps, 62K-line disassemblies) enter the context unsanitized. Input tokens (mostly cache reads) explode: run 7 totaled 60.3M input tokens for 30 trials.

## Evidence
- `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-7/result.json`: `"n_input_tokens": 60294423, "n_cache_tokens": 57303872` for 30 trials.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/result.json`: 11,170,936 input tokens in one 1800s trial; siblings ZrXediE 8.16M, GacsJot 7.56M; make-doom-for-mips kveR2Mi 6.41M, 9na3H9U 4.23M, cawBRSD 4.15M — the two MIPS tasks account for ~46M of run 7's 60.3M.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/agent/fah-sessions/--app--/*.jsonl`: consecutive `shell_job_registry` custom records re-emitted after nearly every assistant message, each listing ALL jobs (60+ entries) with complete command strings (~10KB per record), e.g. entries sh-11…sh-60 all present in one snapshot.
- `make-doom-for-mips__cawBRSD/agent/fa.txt`: repeated whole-file dumps (`cat .../doomgeneric_img.c; ...; sed -n 1690,1968p /app/vm.js`) with no summarization pressure.
- Upstream has related issues (#429 transcript wall, #1073 JSONL disk growth) — this issue covers the model-context/token cost on benches, not disk or UI.

## Proposed fix
- Truncate job cards in the model-visible registry: keep id, state, exit code, first/last ~120 chars of the command; drop stale done/lost cards from the rendered wall after they've been acknowledged (render only running + last K completed).
- Supersede/compact registry snapshots in context instead of re-sending the full history each turn.
- Bench-profile auto-compaction: trigger summarization when context exceeds a token threshold (e.g., 60-80K) or after N minutes, keeping the task text + a rolling summary; make the threshold configurable via env for bench runs.
- Cap single tool outputs at M chars with a `… N chars truncated` marker plus an offset-follow-up affordance.

## Acceptance
1. Deterministic fixture reproducing a 60-job session: total context tokens for the registry shrink by ≥10x; the wall never exceeds K lines.
2. Replay of the jF7GNFh turn profile with the new caps: projected total input tokens ≤ ~3M (vs 11.2M).
3. Compaction events are visible in the session JSONL and preserve task text, ledger obligations, and the latest tool results.

Now the spill changes:

1. `resolveRunSpillsConfig` — env `0` → `const SpillsConfig(enabled: false)`. Note that the notes from a configured section are dropped when env wins (positive value): if the yaml section had notes (e.g., clamped bounds), those notes were printed in `attachSpillWiring` via `spills.notes`. When env overrides, notes from the section are lost. But wait — when env overrides with a positive value, the composed config drops `base.notes`. In `attachSpillWiring`, notes are printed from the composed `spills`. So a yaml section with a misconfigured `headChars: 10` (clamped with a note) would no longer print its note when FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD is also set. Minor, but a behavioral wrinkle: tolerant-parse notes silently swallowed by env override. Actually, notes would be useful to surface. Minor suggestion-level.

2. Also, `resolveRunSpillsConfig` with env set positive does NOT clamp `threshold`... fine, positive int.

3. `buildPreview` change: if body length <= headChars + tailChars, render body once. Note the boundary case: `body.length == headChars + tailChars` renders whole body; else head+tail with omitted marker. In the old code, a body of e.g. 3500 chars with head=2000/tail=2000: head=2000, tail=2000 — overlapping regions (head covers chars 0-2000, tail covers 1500-3500) → duplicated middle 500 chars and omitted = 3500-4000 = negative! So the old code had a real bug for bodies between head+tail/... hmm, actually the old bug fired when body.length < headChars + tailChars (omitted negative). The new code fixes it. Good fix. But is this a behavior change for legacy config (threshold 8192, head 2000, tail 2000)? A spilled body (> 8192 chars) always exceeds 4000, so the new branch only fires when threshold < head+tail, i.e. only under the env knob with small threshold, or a configured small threshold. So legacy behavior byte-identical for the default config. Good.

Wait — one more check: the "covered" branch does not codepoint-check; it renders the whole body, no cut, so no surrogate issue. OK.

# gh-1604: Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone

## Description

## Problem
On long-horizon tasks the model-visible stream accretes without bound: (a) the background-jobs wall re-renders the full shell-job registry — every historical job card with its full command label — after assistant messages, so by job ~60 each turn carries thousands of duplicated tokens forever; (b) no auto-compaction kicks in during 30-min sessions even as the context passes 100K+; (c) single tool results (full-file dumps, 62K-line disassemblies) enter the context unsanitized. Input tokens (mostly cache reads) explode: run 7 totaled 60.3M input tokens for 30 trials.

## Evidence
- `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-7/result.json`: `"n_input_tokens": 60294423, "n_cache_tokens": 57303872` for 30 trials.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/result.json`: 11,170,936 input tokens in one 1800s trial; siblings ZrXediE 8.16M, GacsJot 7.56M; make-doom-for-mips kveR2Mi 6.41M, 9na3H9U 4.23M, cawBRSD 4.15M — the two MIPS tasks account for ~46M of run 7's 60.3M.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/agent/fah-sessions/--app--/*.jsonl`: consecutive `shell_job_registry` custom records re-emitted after nearly every assistant message, each listing ALL jobs (60+ entries) with complete command strings (~10KB per record), e.g. entries sh-11…sh-60 all present in one snapshot.
- `make-doom-for-mips__cawBRSD/agent/fa.txt`: repeated whole-file dumps (`cat .../doomgeneric_img.c; ...; sed -n 1690,1968p /app/vm.js`) with no summarization pressure.
- Upstream has related issues (#429 transcript wall, #1073 JSONL disk growth) — this issue covers the model-context/token cost on benches, not disk or UI.

## Proposed fix
- Truncate job cards in the model-visible registry: keep id, state, exit code, first/last ~120 chars of the command; drop stale done/lost cards from the rendered wall after they've been acknowledged (render only running + last K completed).
- Supersede/compact registry snapshots in context instead of re-sending the full history each turn.
- Bench-profile auto-compaction: trigger summarization when context exceeds a token threshold (e.g., 60-80K) or after N minutes, keeping the task text + a rolling summary; make the threshold configurable via env for bench runs.
- Cap single tool outputs at M chars with a `… N chars truncated` marker plus an offset-follow-up affordance.

## Acceptance
1. Deterministic fixture reproducing a 60-job session: total context tokens for the registry shrink by ≥10x; the wall never exceeds K lines.
2. Replay of the jF7GNFh turn profile with the new caps: projected total input tokens ≤ ~3M (vs 11.2M).
3. Compaction events are visible in the session JSONL and preserve task text, ledger obligations, and the latest tool results.

Shared by the `bash_job` status wall and the job-settle system notice (was: full command in both). - `withCompactionTriggerTokens` raises the compaction reserve so `shouldCompact` fires at the trigger; guards: keep-recent ≤ trigger/2 (a pass always frees), trigger ≥ default threshold is a no-op, junk env is ignored (byte-identical legacy). # gh-1604: Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone

## Description

## Problem
On long-horizon tasks the model-visible stream accretes without bound: (a) the background-jobs wall re-renders the full shell-job registry — every historical job card with its full command label — after assistant messages, so by job ~60 each turn carries thousands of duplicated tokens forever; (b) no auto-compaction kicks in during 30-min sessions even as the context passes 100K+; (c) single tool results (full-file dumps, 62K-line disassemblies) enter the context unsanitized. Input tokens (mostly cache reads) explode: run 7 totaled 60.3M input tokens for 30 trials.

## Evidence
- `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-7/result.json`: `"n_input_tokens": 60294423, "n_cache_tokens": 57303872` for 30 trials.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/result.json`: 11,170,936 input tokens in one 1800s trial; siblings ZrXediE 8.16M, GacsJot 7.56M; make-doom-for-mips kveR2Mi 6.41M, 9na3H9U 4.23M, cawBRSD 4.15M — the two MIPS tasks account for ~46M of run 7's 60.3M.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/agent/fah-sessions/--app--/*.jsonl`: consecutive `shell_job_registry` custom records re-emitted after nearly every assistant message, each listing ALL jobs (60+ entries) with complete command strings (~10KB per record), e.g. entries sh-11…sh-60 all present in one snapshot.
- `make-doom-for-mips__cawBRSD/agent/fa.txt`: repeated whole-file dumps (`cat .../doomgeneric_img.c; ...; sed -n 1690,1968p /app/vm.js`) with no summarization pressure.
- Upstream has related issues (#429 transcript wall, #1073 JSONL disk growth) — this issue covers the model-context/token cost on benches, not disk or UI.

## Proposed fix
- Truncate job cards in the model-visible registry: keep id, state, exit code, first/last ~120 chars of the command; drop stale done/lost cards from the rendered wall after they've been acknowledged (render only running + last K completed).
- Supersede/compact registry snapshots in context instead of re-sending the full history each turn.
- Bench-profile auto-compaction: trigger summarization when context exceeds a token threshold (e.g., 60-80K) or after N minutes, keeping the task text + a rolling summary; make the threshold configurable via env for bench runs.
- Cap single tool outputs at M chars with a `… N chars truncated` marker plus an offset-follow-up affordance.

## Acceptance
1. Deterministic fixture reproducing a 60-job session: total context tokens for the registry shrink by ≥10x; the wall never exceeds K lines.
2. Replay of the jF7GNFh turn profile with the new caps: projected total input tokens ≤ ~3M (vs 11.2M).
3. Compaction events are visible in the session JSONL and preserve task text, ledger obligations, and the latest tool results.

# gh-1604: Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone

## Description

## Problem
On long-horizon tasks the model-visible stream accretes without bound: (a) the background-jobs wall re-renders the full shell-job registry — every historical job card with its full command label — after assistant messages, so by job ~60 each turn carries thousands of duplicated tokens forever; (b) no auto-compaction kicks in during 30-min sessions even as the context passes 100K+; (c) single tool results (full-file dumps, 62K-line disassemblies) enter the context unsanitized. Input tokens (mostly cache reads) explode: run 7 totaled 60.3M input tokens for 30 trials.

## Evidence
- `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-7/result.json`: `"n_input_tokens": 60294423, "n_cache_tokens": 57303872` for 30 trials.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/result.json`: 11,170,936 input tokens in one 1800s trial; siblings ZrXediE 8.16M, GacsJot 7.56M; make-doom-for-mips kveR2Mi 6.41M, 9na3H9U 4.23M, cawBRSD 4.15M — the two MIPS tasks account for ~46M of run 7's 60.3M.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/agent/fah-sessions/--app--/*.jsonl`: consecutive `shell_job_registry` custom records re-emitted after nearly every assistant message, each listing ALL jobs (60+ entries) with complete command strings (~10KB per record), e.g. entries sh-11…sh-60 all present in one snapshot.
- `make-doom-for-mips__cawBRSD/agent/fa.txt`: repeated whole-file dumps (`cat .../doomgeneric_img.c; ...; sed -n 1690,1968p /app/vm.js`) with no summarization pressure.
- Upstream has related issues (#429 transcript wall, #1073 JSONL disk growth) — this issue covers the model-context/token cost on benches, not disk or UI.

## Proposed fix
- Truncate job cards in the model-visible registry: keep id, state, exit code, first/last ~120 chars of the command; drop stale done/lost cards from the rendered wall after they've been acknowledged (render only running + last K completed).
- Supersede/compact registry snapshots in context instead of re-sending the full history each turn.
- Bench-profile auto-compaction: trigger summarization when context exceeds a token threshold (e.g., 60-80K) or after N minutes, keeping the task text + a rolling summary; make the threshold configurable via env for bench runs.
- Cap single tool outputs at M chars with a `… N chars truncated` marker plus an offset-follow-up affordance.

## Acceptance
1. Deterministic fixture reproducing a 60-job session: total context tokens for the registry shrink by ≥10x; the wall never exceeds K lines.
2. Replay of the jF7GNFh turn profile with the new caps: projected total input tokens ≤ ~3M (vs 11.2M).
3. Compaction events are visible in the session JSONL and preserve task text, ledger obligations, and the latest tool results.

Shared by the `bash_job` status wall and the job-settle system notice (was: full command in both). - `withCompactionTriggerTokens` raises the compaction reserve so `shouldCompact` fires at the trigger; guards: keep-recent ≤ trigger/2 (a pass always frees), trigger ≥ default threshold is a no-op, junk env is ignored (byte-identical legacy). Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override. - Task preservation rides the existing mechanisms, verified end-to-end: the checkpoint summarizer prompt carries the task text; the obligations-ledger block and the latest tool result (protected tail) survive in the post-compaction projection; the checkpoint record is visible in the session JSONL. - `resolveRunSpillsConfig` composes the env knob over the yaml section (env wins; `0` disables); `buildPreview` no longer duplicates a body smaller than its head+tail bounds. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/tools/shell_job_command_label_test.dart \ test/compaction/bench_trigger_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart \ test/spill/spill_env_test.dart ``` `agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` is the end-to-end proof: with the env set the compaction fires mid-run where the default (183k-token trigger) never would, every later turn request stays under the bench trigger, and the control run (no env) compacts nothing at the same sizes. ### Coverage notes - AC1 is covered by the deterministic fixture in `shell_job_command_label_test.dart`: a 60-job registry renders ≥10x less model-visible material than the pre-fix shape, and the status wall stays within K lines (running + last 20 exited + overflow tail). - AC2's full turn-profile replay was not built; the per-request bound is asserted directly instead (every post-crossing turn request ≤ the trigger). - AC3 is covered by the CLI test (JSONL event, task text in the summarizer request, ledger + latest tool result in the projection).

# gh-1604: Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone

## Description

## Problem
On long-horizon tasks the model-visible stream accretes without bound: (a) the background-jobs wall re-renders the full shell-job registry — every historical job card with its full command label — after assistant messages, so by job ~60 each turn carries thousands of duplicated tokens forever; (b) no auto-compaction kicks in during 30-min sessions even as the context passes 100K+; (c) single tool results (full-file dumps, 62K-line disassemblies) enter the context unsanitized. Input tokens (mostly cache reads) explode: run 7 totaled 60.3M input tokens for 30 trials.

## Evidence
- `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-7/result.json`: `"n_input_tokens": 60294423, "n_cache_tokens": 57303872` for 30 trials.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/result.json`: 11,170,936 input tokens in one 1800s trial; siblings ZrXediE 8.16M, GacsJot 7.56M; make-doom-for-mips kveR2Mi 6.41M, 9na3H9U 4.23M, cawBRSD 4.15M — the two MIPS tasks account for ~46M of run 7's 60.3M.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/agent/fah-sessions/--app--/*.jsonl`: consecutive `shell_job_registry` custom records re-emitted after nearly every assistant message, each listing ALL jobs (60+ entries) with complete command strings (~10KB per record), e.g. entries sh-11…sh-60 all present in one snapshot.
- `make-doom-for-mips__cawBRSD/agent/fa.txt`: repeated whole-file dumps (`cat .../doomgeneric_img.c; ...; sed -n 1690,1968p /app/vm.js`) with no summarization pressure.
- Upstream has related issues (#429 transcript wall, #1073 JSONL disk growth) — this issue covers the model-context/token cost on benches, not disk or UI.

## Proposed fix
- Truncate job cards in the model-visible registry: keep id, state, exit code, first/last ~120 chars of the command; drop stale done/lost cards from the rendered wall after they've been acknowledged (render only running + last K completed).
- Supersede/compact registry snapshots in context instead of re-sending the full history each turn.
- Bench-profile auto-compaction: trigger summarization when context exceeds a token threshold (e.g., 60-80K) or after N minutes, keeping the task text + a rolling summary; make the threshold configurable via env for bench runs.
- Cap single tool outputs at M chars with a `… N chars truncated` marker plus an offset-follow-up affordance.

## Acceptance
1. Deterministic fixture reproducing a 60-job session: total context tokens for the registry shrink by ≥10x; the wall never exceeds K lines.
2. Replay of the jF7GNFh turn profile with the new caps: projected total input tokens ≤ ~3M (vs 11.2M).
3. Compaction events are visible in the session JSONL and preserve task text, ledger obligations, and the latest tool results.

Now the spill changes:

1. `resolveRunSpillsConfig` — env `0` → `const SpillsConfig(enabled: false)`. Note that the notes from a configured section are dropped when env wins (positive value): if the yaml section had notes (e.g., clamped bounds), those notes were printed in `attachSpillWiring` via `spills.notes`. When env overrides, notes from the section are lost. But wait — when env overrides with a positive value, the composed config drops `base.notes`. In `attachSpillWiring`, notes are printed from the composed `spills`. So a yaml section with a misconfigured `headChars: 10` (clamped with a note) would no longer print its note when FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD is also set. Minor, but a behavioral wrinkle: tolerant-parse notes silently swallowed by env override. Actually, notes would be useful to surface. Minor suggestion-level.

2. Also, `resolveRunSpillsConfig` with env set positive does NOT clamp `threshold`... fine, positive int.

3. `buildPreview` change: if body length <= headChars + tailChars, render body once. # gh-1604: Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone

## Description

## Problem
On long-horizon tasks the model-visible stream accretes without bound: (a) the background-jobs wall re-renders the full shell-job registry — every historical job card with its full command label — after assistant messages, so by job ~60 each turn carries thousands of duplicated tokens forever; (b) no auto-compaction kicks in during 30-min sessions even as the context passes 100K+; (c) single tool results (full-file dumps, 62K-line disassemblies) enter the context unsanitized. Input tokens (mostly cache reads) explode: run 7 totaled 60.3M input tokens for 30 trials.

## Evidence
- `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-7/result.json`: `"n_input_tokens": 60294423, "n_cache_tokens": 57303872` for 30 trials.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/result.json`: 11,170,936 input tokens in one 1800s trial; siblings ZrXediE 8.16M, GacsJot 7.56M; make-doom-for-mips kveR2Mi 6.41M, 9na3H9U 4.23M, cawBRSD 4.15M — the two MIPS tasks account for ~46M of run 7's 60.3M.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/agent/fah-sessions/--app--/*.jsonl`: consecutive `shell_job_registry` custom records re-emitted after nearly every assistant message, each listing ALL jobs (60+ entries) with complete command strings (~10KB per record), e.g. entries sh-11…sh-60 all present in one snapshot.
- `make-doom-for-mips__cawBRSD/agent/fa.txt`: repeated whole-file dumps (`cat .../doomgeneric_img.c; ...; sed -n 1690,1968p /app/vm.js`) with no summarization pressure.
- Upstream has related issues (#429 transcript wall, #1073 JSONL disk growth) — this issue covers the model-context/token cost on benches, not disk or UI.

## Proposed fix
- Truncate job cards in the model-visible registry: keep id, state, exit code, first/last ~120 chars of the command; drop stale done/lost cards from the rendered wall after they've been acknowledged (render only running + last K completed).
- Supersede/compact registry snapshots in context instead of re-sending the full history each turn.
- Bench-profile auto-compaction: trigger summarization when context exceeds a token threshold (e.g., 60-80K) or after N minutes, keeping the task text + a rolling summary; make the threshold configurable via env for bench runs.
- Cap single tool outputs at M chars with a `… N chars truncated` marker plus an offset-follow-up affordance.

## Acceptance
1. Deterministic fixture reproducing a 60-job session: total context tokens for the registry shrink by ≥10x; the wall never exceeds K lines.
2. Replay of the jF7GNFh turn profile with the new caps: projected total input tokens ≤ ~3M (vs 11.2M).
3. Compaction events are visible in the session JSONL and preserve task text, ledger obligations, and the latest tool results.

# gh-1604: Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone

## Description

## Problem
On long-horizon tasks the model-visible stream accretes without bound: (a) the background-jobs wall re-renders the full shell-job registry — every historical job card with its full command label — after assistant messages, so by job ~60 each turn carries thousands of duplicated tokens forever; (b) no auto-compaction kicks in during 30-min sessions even as the context passes 100K+; (c) single tool results (full-file dumps, 62K-line disassemblies) enter the context unsanitized. Input tokens (mostly cache reads) explode: run 7 totaled 60.3M input tokens for 30 trials.

## Evidence
- `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-7/result.json`: `"n_input_tokens": 60294423, "n_cache_tokens": 57303872` for 30 trials.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/result.json`: 11,170,936 input tokens in one 1800s trial; siblings ZrXediE 8.16M, GacsJot 7.56M; make-doom-for-mips kveR2Mi 6.41M, 9na3H9U 4.23M, cawBRSD 4.15M — the two MIPS tasks account for ~46M of run 7's 60.3M.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/agent/fah-sessions/--app--/*.jsonl`: consecutive `shell_job_registry` custom records re-emitted after nearly every assistant message, each listing ALL jobs (60+ entries) with complete command strings (~10KB per record), e.g. entries sh-11…sh-60 all present in one snapshot.
- `make-doom-for-mips__cawBRSD/agent/fa.txt`: repeated whole-file dumps (`cat .../doomgeneric_img.c; ...; sed -n 1690,1968p /app/vm.js`) with no summarization pressure.
- Upstream has related issues (#429 transcript wall, #1073 JSONL disk growth) — this issue covers the model-context/token cost on benches, not disk or UI.

## Proposed fix
- Truncate job cards in the model-visible registry: keep id, state, exit code, first/last ~120 chars of the command; drop stale done/lost cards from the rendered wall after they've been acknowledged (render only running + last K completed).
- Supersede/compact registry snapshots in context instead of re-sending the full history each turn.
- Bench-profile auto-compaction: trigger summarization when context exceeds a token threshold (e.g., 60-80K) or after N minutes, keeping the task text + a rolling summary; make the threshold configurable via env for bench runs.
- Cap single tool outputs at M chars with a `… N chars truncated` marker plus an offset-follow-up affordance.

## Acceptance
1. Deterministic fixture reproducing a 60-job session: total context tokens for the registry shrink by ≥10x; the wall never exceeds K lines.
2. Replay of the jF7GNFh turn profile with the new caps: projected total input tokens ≤ ~3M (vs 11.2M).
3. Compaction events are visible in the session JSONL and preserve task text, ledger obligations, and the latest tool results.

Shared by the `bash_job` status wall and the job-settle system notice (was: full command in both). - `withCompactionTriggerTokens` raises the compaction reserve so `shouldCompact` fires at the trigger; guards: keep-recent ≤ trigger/2 (a pass always frees), trigger ≥ default threshold is a no-op, junk env is ignored (byte-identical legacy). Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override. - Task preservation rides the existing mechanisms, verified end-to-end: the checkpoint summarizer prompt carries the task text; the obligations-ledger block and the latest tool result (protected tail) survive in the post-compaction projection; the checkpoint record is visible in the session JSONL. - `resolveRunSpillsConfig` composes the env knob over the yaml section (env wins; `0` disables); `buildPreview` no longer duplicates a body smaller than its head+tail bounds. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/tools/shell_job_command_label_test.dart \ test/compaction/bench_trigger_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart \ test/spill/spill_env_test.dart ``` `agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` is the end-to-end proof: with the env set the compaction fires mid-run where the default (183k-token trigger) never would, every later turn request stays under the bench trigger, and the control run (no env) compacts nothing at the same sizes. ### Coverage notes - AC1 is covered by the deterministic fixture in `shell_job_command_label_test.dart`: a 60-job registry renders ≥10x less model-visible material than the pre-fix shape, and the status wall stays within K lines (running + last 20 exited + overflow tail). - AC2's full turn-profile replay was not built; the per-request bound is asserted directly instead (every post-crossing turn request ≤ the trigger). - AC3 is covered by the CLI test (JSONL event, task text in the summarizer request, ledger + latest tool result in the projection).

# gh-1604: Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone

## Description

## Problem
On long-horizon tasks the model-visible stream accretes without bound: (a) the background-jobs wall re-renders the full shell-job registry — every historical job card with its full command label — after assistant messages, so by job ~60 each turn carries thousands of duplicated tokens forever; (b) no auto-compaction kicks in during 30-min sessions even as the context passes 100K+; (c) single tool results (full-file dumps, 62K-line disassemblies) enter the context unsanitized. Input tokens (mostly cache reads) explode: run 7 totaled 60.3M input tokens for 30 trials.

## Evidence
- `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-7/result.json`: `"n_input_tokens": 60294423, "n_cache_tokens": 57303872` for 30 trials.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/result.json`: 11,170,936 input tokens in one 1800s trial; siblings ZrXediE 8.16M, GacsJot 7.56M; make-doom-for-mips kveR2Mi 6.41M, 9na3H9U 4.23M, cawBRSD 4.15M — the two MIPS tasks account for ~46M of run 7's 60.3M.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/agent/fah-sessions/--app--/*.jsonl`: consecutive `shell_job_registry` custom records re-emitted after nearly every assistant message, each listing ALL jobs (60+ entries) with complete command strings (~10KB per record), e.g. entries sh-11…sh-60 all present in one snapshot.
- `make-doom-for-mips__cawBRSD/agent/fa.txt`: repeated whole-file dumps (`cat .../doomgeneric_img.c; ...; sed -n 1690,1968p /app/vm.js`) with no summarization pressure.
- Upstream has related issues (#429 transcript wall, #1073 JSONL disk growth) — this issue covers the model-context/token cost on benches, not disk or UI.

## Proposed fix
- Truncate job cards in the model-visible registry: keep id, state, exit code, first/last ~120 chars of the command; drop stale done/lost cards from the rendered wall after they've been acknowledged (render only running + last K completed).
- Supersede/compact registry snapshots in context instead of re-sending the full history each turn.
- Bench-profile auto-compaction: trigger summarization when context exceeds a token threshold (e.g., 60-80K) or after N minutes, keeping the task text + a rolling summary; make the threshold configurable via env for bench runs.
- Cap single tool outputs at M chars with a `… N chars truncated` marker plus an offset-follow-up affordance.

## Acceptance
1. Deterministic fixture reproducing a 60-job session: total context tokens for the registry shrink by ≥10x; the wall never exceeds K lines.
2. Replay of the jF7GNFh turn profile with the new caps: projected total input tokens ≤ ~3M (vs 11.2M).
3. Compaction events are visible in the session JSONL and preserve task text, ledger obligations, and the latest tool results.

# gh-1604: Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone

## Description

## Problem
On long-horizon tasks the model-visible stream accretes without bound: (a) the background-jobs wall re-renders the full shell-job registry — every historical job card with its full command label — after assistant messages, so by job ~60 each turn carries thousands of duplicated tokens forever; (b) no auto-compaction kicks in during 30-min sessions even as the context passes 100K+; (c) single tool results (full-file dumps, 62K-line disassemblies) enter the context unsanitized. Input tokens (mostly cache reads) explode: run 7 totaled 60.3M input tokens for 30 trials.

## Evidence
- `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-7/result.json`: `"n_input_tokens": 60294423, "n_cache_tokens": 57303872` for 30 trials.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/result.json`: 11,170,936 input tokens in one 1800s trial; siblings ZrXediE 8.16M, GacsJot 7.56M; make-doom-for-mips kveR2Mi 6.41M, 9na3H9U 4.23M, cawBRSD 4.15M — the two MIPS tasks account for ~46M of run 7's 60.3M.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/agent/fah-sessions/--app--/*.jsonl`: consecutive `shell_job_registry` custom records re-emitted after nearly every assistant message, each listing ALL jobs (60+ entries) with complete command strings (~10KB per record), e.g. entries sh-11…sh-60 all present in one snapshot.
- `make-doom-for-mips__cawBRSD/agent/fa.txt`: repeated whole-file dumps (`cat .../doomgeneric_img.c; ...; sed -n 1690,1968p /app/vm.js`) with no summarization pressure.
- Upstream has related issues (#429 transcript wall, #1073 JSONL disk growth) — this issue covers the model-context/token cost on benches, not disk or UI.

## Proposed fix
- Truncate job cards in the model-visible registry: keep id, state, exit code, first/last ~120 chars of the command; drop stale done/lost cards from the rendered wall after they've been acknowledged (render only running + last K completed).
- Supersede/compact registry snapshots in context instead of re-sending the full history each turn.
- Bench-profile auto-compaction: trigger summarization when context exceeds a token threshold (e.g., 60-80K) or after N minutes, keeping the task text + a rolling summary; make the threshold configurable via env for bench runs.
- Cap single tool outputs at M chars with a `… N chars truncated` marker plus an offset-follow-up affordance.

## Acceptance
1. Deterministic fixture reproducing a 60-job session: total context tokens for the registry shrink by ≥10x; the wall never exceeds K lines.
2. Replay of the jF7GNFh turn profile with the new caps: projected total input tokens ≤ ~3M (vs 11.2M).
3. Compaction events are visible in the session JSONL and preserve task text, ledger obligations, and the latest tool results.

Shared by the `bash_job` status wall and the job-settle system notice (was: full command in both). - `withCompactionTriggerTokens` raises the compaction reserve so `shouldCompact` fires at the trigger; guards: keep-recent ≤ trigger/2 (a pass always frees), trigger ≥ default threshold is a no-op, junk env is ignored (byte-identical legacy). Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override. - Task preservation rides the existing mechanisms, verified end-to-end: the checkpoint summarizer prompt carries the task text; the obligations-ledger block and the latest tool result (protected tail) survive in the post-compaction projection; the checkpoint record is visible in the session JSONL. - `resolveRunSpillsConfig` composes the env knob over the yaml section (env wins; `0` disables); `buildPreview` no longer duplicates a body smaller than its head+tail bounds. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/tools/shell_job_command_label_test.dart \ test/compaction/bench_trigger_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart \ test/spill/spill_env_test.dart ``` `agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` is the end-to-end proof: with the env set the compaction fires mid-run where the default (183k-token trigger) never would, every later turn request stays under the bench trigger, and the control run (no env) compacts nothing at the same sizes. ### Coverage notes - AC1 is covered by the deterministic fixture in `shell_job_command_label_test.dart`: a 60-job registry renders ≥10x less model-visible material than the pre-fix shape, and the status wall stays within K lines (running + last 20 exited + overflow tail). - AC2's full turn-profile replay was not built; the per-request bound is asserted directly instead (every post-crossing turn request ≤ the trigger). - AC3 is covered by the CLI test (JSONL event, task text in the summarizer request, ledger + latest tool result in the projection).
