blocks.text:
# gh-1604: Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone

## Description

## Problem
On long-horizon tasks the model-visible stream accretes without bound: (a) the background-jobs wall re-renders the full shell-job registry — every historical job card with its full command label — after assistant messages, so by job ~60 each turn carries thousands of duplicated tokens forever; (b) no auto-compaction kicks in during 30-min sessions even as the context passes 100K+; (c) single tool results (full-file dumps, 62K-line disassemblies) enter the context unsanitized. Input tokens (mostly cache reads) explode: run 7 totaled 60.3M input tokens for 30 trials.

## Evidence
- `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-7/result.json`: `"n_input_tokens": 60294423, "n_cache_tokens": 57303872` for 30 trials.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/result.json`: 11,170,936 input tokens in one 1800s trial; siblings ZrXediE 8.16M, GacsJot 7.56M; make-doom-for-mips kveR2Mi 6.41M, 9na3H9U 4.23M, cawBRSD 4.15M — the two MIPS tasks account for ~46M of run 7's 60.3M.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/agent/fah-sessions/--app--/*.jsonl`: consecutive `shell_job_registry` custom records re-emitted after nearly every assistant message, each listing ALL jobs (60+ entries) with complete command strings (~10KB per record), e.g. entries sh-11…sh-60 all present in one snapshot.
- `make-doom-for-mips__cawBRSD/agent/fa.txt`: repeated whole-file dumps (`cat .../doomgeneric_img.c; ...; sed -n 1690,1968p /app/vm.js`) with no summarization pressure.
- Upstream has related issues (#429 transcript wall, #1073 JSONL disk growth) — this issue covers the model-context/token cost on benches, not disk or UI.

## Proposed fix
- Truncate job cards in the model-visible registry: keep id, state, exit code, first/last ~120 chars of the command; drop stale done/lost cards from the rendered wall after they've been acknowledged (render only running + last K completed).
- Supersede/compact registry snapshots in context instead of re-sending the full history each turn.
- Bench-profile auto-compaction: trigger summarization when context exceeds a token threshold (e.g., 60-80K) or after N minutes, keeping the task text + a rolling summary; make the threshold configurable via env for bench runs.
- Cap single tool outputs at M chars with a `… N chars truncated` marker plus an offset-follow-up affordance.

## Acceptance
1. Deterministic fixture reproducing a 60-job session: total context tokens for the registry shrink by ≥10x; the wall never exceeds K lines.
2. Replay of the jF7GNFh turn profile with the new caps: projected total input tokens ≤ ~3M (vs 11.2M).
3. Compaction events are visible in the session JSONL and preserve task text, ledger obligations, and the latest tool results.

# gh-1604: Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone

## Description

## Problem
On long-horizon tasks the model-visible stream accretes without bound: (a) the background-jobs wall re-renders the full shell-job registry — every historical job card with its full command label — after assistant messages, so by job ~60 each turn carries thousands of duplicated tokens forever; (b) no auto-compaction kicks in during 30-min sessions even as the context passes 100K+; (c) single tool results (full-file dumps, 62K-line disassemblies) enter the context unsanitized. Input tokens (mostly cache reads) explode: run 7 totaled 60.3M input tokens for 30 trials.

## Evidence
- `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-7/result.json`: `"n_input_tokens": 60294423, "n_cache_tokens": 57303872` for 30 trials.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/result.json`: 11,170,936 input tokens in one 1800s trial; siblings ZrXediE 8.16M, GacsJot 7.56M; make-doom-for-mips kveR2Mi 6.41M, 9na3H9U 4.23M, cawBRSD 4.15M — the two MIPS tasks account for ~46M of run 7's 60.3M.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/agent/fah-sessions/--app--/*.jsonl`: consecutive `shell_job_registry` custom records re-emitted after nearly every assistant message, each listing ALL jobs (60+ entries) with complete command strings (~10KB per record), e.g. entries sh-11…sh-60 all present in one snapshot.
- `make-doom-for-mips__cawBRSD/agent/fa.txt`: repeated whole-file dumps (`cat .../doomgeneric_img.c; ...; sed -n 1690,1968p /app/vm.js`) with no summarization pressure.
- Upstream has related issues (#429 transcript wall, #1073 JSONL disk growth) — this issue covers the model-context/token cost on benches, not disk or UI.

## Proposed fix
- Truncate job cards in the model-visible registry: keep id, state, exit code, first/last ~120 chars of the command; drop stale done/lost cards from the rendered wall after they've been acknowledged (render only running + last K completed).
- Supersede/compact registry snapshots in context instead of re-sending the full history each turn.
- Bench-profile auto-compaction: trigger summarization when context exceeds a token threshold (e.g., 60-80K) or after N minutes, keeping the task text + a rolling summary; make the threshold configurable via env for bench runs.
- Cap single tool outputs at M chars with a `… N chars truncated` marker plus an offset-follow-up affordance.

## Acceptance
1. Deterministic fixture reproducing a 60-job session: total context tokens for the registry shrink by ≥10x; the wall never exceeds K lines.
2. Replay of the jF7GNFh turn profile with the new caps: projected total input tokens ≤ ~3M (vs 11.2M).
3. Compaction events are visible in the session JSONL and preserve task text, ledger obligations, and the latest tool results.

# Pull Request Information - **PR #**: 1612 - **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1612 - **Title**: gh-1604 Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone - **Author**: ai-teammate - **Branch**: `ai/gh-1604` → `main` - **State**: open - **Files Changed**: 12 - **Additions**: +1118 - **Deletions**: -23 - **Created**: 2026-10-14T14:50:41Z - **Updated**: 2026-10-14T15:29:57Z ## PR Description Closes #1604 ### What changed Bounds the model-visible cost of long bench runs (gh-1604): background-job commands are truncated to a bounded label on every model-facing surface, a bench env knob (`FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS`) lowers the auto-compaction trigger to an absolute context size so long trials compact mid-run instead of accreting, and a `FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD` env knob enables the tool-output spill cap per run without a config file. ### Key decisions - New `shellJobCommandLabel` (pure, surrogate-safe): single-line commands keep the first/last 120 chars of the whitespace-flattened command with a `[…N chars…]` marker naming the true omitted size; multi-line commands keep the bounded FIRST LINE only (issue #599 RED contract — a heredoc body is never a transcript row source, and a flattened head or whole-command tail would echo body lines back through every settle notice). Shared by the `bash_job` status wall and the job-settle system notice (was: full command in both). - `withCompactionTriggerTokens` raises the compaction reserve so `shouldCompact` fires at the trigger; guards: keep-recent ≤ trigger/2 (a pass always frees), trigger ≥ default threshold is a no-op, junk env is ignored (byte-identical legacy). Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override. - Task preservation rides the existing mechanisms, verified end-to-end: the checkpoint summarizer prompt carries the task text; the obligations-ledger block and the latest tool result (protected tail) survive in the post-compaction projection; the checkpoint record is visible in the session JSONL. - `resolveRunSpillsConfig` composes the env knob over the yaml section (env wins; `0` disables); `buildPreview` no longer duplicates a body smaller than its head+tail bounds. ### How to verify ```bash dart test test/tools/shell_job_command_label_test.dart \ test/compaction/bench_trigger_test.dart \ test/cli/agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart \ test/spill/spill_env_test.dart ``` `agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` is the end-to-end proof: with the env set the compaction fires mid-run where the default (183k-token trigger) never would, every later turn request stays under the bench trigger, and the control run (no env) compacts nothing at the same sizes. ### Coverage notes - AC1 is covered by the deterministic fixture in `shell_job_command_label_test.dart`: a 60-job registry renders ≥10x less model-visible material than the pre-fix shape, and the status wall stays within K lines (running + last 20 exited + overflow tail). - AC2's full turn-profile replay was not built; the per-request bound is asserted directly instead (every post-crossing turn request ≤ the trigger). - AC3 is covered by the CLI test (JSONL event, task text in the summarizer request, ledger + latest tool result in the projection).
Architecture ```mermaid flowchart TD ENV["bench env knobs"] --> BT["resolveBenchCompactionSettings"] BT --> GATE["shouldCompact fires at the trigger"] GATE --> ENG["structured compaction (existing)"] ENG --> CKPT["CompactCheckpointRecord in JSONL
(task text → summarizer prompt;
ledger + latest tool results → protected tail)"] JOBS["bash background jobs"] --> LBL["shellJobCommandLabel"] LBL --> WALL["bash_job status wall + settle notice"] SPILL["FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD"] --> RC["resolveRunSpillsConfig"] RC --> HOOKS["spill hooks (existing)"] ```

# gh-1604: Bound the background-jobs wall and compact long bench sessions: run 7 burned 60.3M input tokens, ~46M in two MIPS tasks alone

## Description

## Problem
On long-horizon tasks the model-visible stream accretes without bound: (a) the background-jobs wall re-renders the full shell-job registry — every historical job card with its full command label — after assistant messages, so by job ~60 each turn carries thousands of duplicated tokens forever; (b) no auto-compaction kicks in during 30-min sessions even as the context passes 100K+; (c) single tool results (full-file dumps, 62K-line disassemblies) enter the context unsanitized. Input tokens (mostly cache reads) explode: run 7 totaled 60.3M input tokens for 30 trials.

## Evidence
- `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-7/result.json`: `"n_input_tokens": 60294423, "n_cache_tokens": 57303872` for 30 trials.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/result.json`: 11,170,936 input tokens in one 1800s trial; siblings ZrXediE 8.16M, GacsJot 7.56M; make-doom-for-mips kveR2Mi 6.41M, 9na3H9U 4.23M, cawBRSD 4.15M — the two MIPS tasks account for ~46M of run 7's 60.3M.
- `make-mips-interpreter__jF7GNFh/agent/fah-sessions/--app--/*.jsonl`: consecutive `shell_job_registry` custom records re-emitted after nearly every assistant message, each listing ALL jobs (60+ entries) with complete command strings (~10KB per record), e.g. entries sh-11…sh-60 all present in one snapshot.
- `make-doom-for-mips__cawBRSD/agent/fa.txt`: repeated whole-file dumps (`cat .../doomgeneric_img.c; ...; sed -n 1690,1968p /app/vm.js`) with no summarization pressure.
- Upstream has related issues (#429 transcript wall, #1073 JSONL disk growth) — this issue covers the model-context/token cost on benches, not disk or UI.

## Proposed fix
- Truncate job cards in the model-visible registry: keep id, state, exit code, first/last ~120 chars of the command; drop stale done/lost cards from the rendered wall after they've been acknowledged (render only running + last K completed).
- Supersede/compact registry snapshots in context instead of re-sending the full history each turn.
- Bench-profile auto-compaction: trigger summarization when context exceeds a token threshold (e.g., 60-80K) or after N minutes, keeping the task text + a rolling summary; make the threshold configurable via env for bench runs.
- Cap single tool outputs at M chars with a `… N chars truncated` marker plus an offset-follow-up affordance.

## Acceptance
1. Deterministic fixture reproducing a 60-job session: total context tokens for the registry shrink by ≥10x; the wall never exceeds K lines.
2. Replay of the jF7GNFh turn profile with the new caps: projected total input tokens ≤ ~3M (vs 11.2M).
3. Compaction events are visible in the session JSONL and preserve task text, ledger obligations, and the latest tool results.

Now the spill changes:

1. `resolveRunSpillsConfig` — env `0` → `const SpillsConfig(enabled: false)`. Note that the notes from a configured section are dropped when env wins (positive value): if the yaml section had notes (e.g., clamped bounds), those notes were printed in `attachSpillWiring` via `spills.notes`. When env overrides, notes from the section are lost. But wait — when env overrides with a positive value, the composed config drops `base.notes`. Now the spill changes:

1. `resolveRunSpillsConfig` — env `0` → `const SpillsConfig(enabled: false)`. Note that the notes from a configured section are dropped when env wins (positive value): if the yaml section had notes (e.g., clamped bounds), those notes were printed in `attachSpillWiring` via `spills.notes`. When env overrides, notes from the section are lost. But wait — when env overrides with a positive value, the composed config drops `base.notes`. In `attachSpillWiring`, notes are printed from the composed `spills`. So a yaml section with a misconfigured `headChars: 10` (clamped with a note) would no longer print its note when FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD is also set. Minor, but a behavioral wrinkle: tolerant-parse notes silently swallowed by env override. Actually, notes would be useful to surface. Minor suggestion-level.

2. Also, `resolveRunSpillsConfig` with env set positive does NOT clamp `threshold`... fine, positive int.

3. `buildPreview` change: if body length <= headChars + tailChars, render body once. Note the boundary case: `body.length == headChars + tailChars` renders whole body; else head+tail with omitted marker. In the old code, a body of e.g. 3500 chars with head=2000/tail=2000: head=2000, tail=2000 — overlapping regions (head covers chars 0-2000, tail covers 1500-3500) → duplicated middle 500 chars and omitted = 3500-4000 = negative! So the old code had a real bug for bodies between head+tail/... hmm, actually the old bug fired when body.length < headChars + tailChars (omitted negative). The new code fixes it. Good fix. But is this a behavior change for legacy config (threshold 8192, head 2000, tail 2000)? A spilled body (> 8192 chars) always exceeds 4000, so the new branch only fires when threshold < head+tail, i.e. only under the env knob with small threshold, or a configured small threshold. So legacy behavior byte-identical for the default config. Good.

Now the spill changes:

1. `resolveRunSpillsConfig` — env `0` → `const SpillsConfig(enabled: false)`. Note that the notes from a configured section are dropped when env wins (positive value): if the yaml section had notes (e.g., clamped bounds), those notes were printed in `attachSpillWiring` via `spills.notes`. When env overrides, notes from the section are lost. But wait — when env overrides with a positive value, the composed config drops `base.notes`. In `attachSpillWiring`, notes are printed from the composed `spills`. So a yaml section with a misconfigured `headChars: 10` (clamped with a note) would no longer print its note when FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD is also set. Minor, but a behavioral wrinkle: tolerant-parse notes silently swallowed by env override. Actually, notes would be useful to surface. Minor suggestion-level.

2. Also, `resolveRunSpillsConfig` with env set positive does NOT clamp `threshold`... fine, positive int.

3. `buildPreview` change: if body length <= headChars + tailChars, render body once. Note the boundary case: `body.length == headChars + tailChars` renders whole body; else head+tail with omitted marker. In the old code, a body of e.g. 3500 chars with head=2000/tail=2000: head=2000, tail=2000 — overlapping regions (head covers chars 0-2000, tail covers 1500-3500) → duplicated middle 500 chars and omitted = 3500-4000 = negative! So the old code had a real bug for bodies between head+tail/... hmm, actually the old bug fired when body.length < headChars + tailChars (omitted negative). The new code fixes it. Good fix. But is this a behavior change for legacy config (threshold 8192, head 2000, tail 2000)? A spilled body (> 8192 chars) always exceeds 4000, so the new branch only fires when threshold < head+tail, i.e. only under the env knob with small threshold, or a configured small threshold. So legacy behavior byte-identical for the default config. Good.

Wait — one more check: the "covered" branch does not codepoint-check; it renders the whole body, no cut, so no surrogate issue. OK.

4. `agent_cli_spill.dart`: the new log line prints `[spills] enabled via FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD=... (threshold N chars)`. Note: this only prints when `config.spills == null`. If config.spills != null and env overrides the threshold, note about the env override — minor.

Also check: `attachSpillWiring` — where is it called from? If `config.spills == null` and env unset → spills = null → no attach (legacy). Good.

But wait — is `attachSpillWiring` the only place `config.spills` is consumed? Let me check other consumers of `config.spills` to make sure the env knob composes everywhere (e.g., the wire serve path or app path may read config.spills directly).

Now the spill changes:

Note that the notes from a configured section are dropped when env wins (positive value): if the yaml section had notes (e.g., clamped bounds), those notes were printed in `attachSpillWiring` via `spills.notes`. When env overrides, notes from the section are lost. But wait — when env overrides with a positive value, the composed config drops `base.notes`. In `attachSpillWiring`, notes are printed from the composed `spills`. So a yaml section with a misconfigured `headChars: 10` (clamped with a note) would no longer print its note when FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD is also set. Note the boundary case: `body.length == headChars + tailChars` renders whole body; else head+tail with omitted marker. Now the spill changes:

1. `resolveRunSpillsConfig` — env `0` → `const SpillsConfig(enabled: false)`. Note that the notes from a configured section are dropped when env wins (positive value): if the yaml section had notes (e.g., clamped bounds), those notes were printed in `attachSpillWiring` via `spills.notes`. When env overrides, notes from the section are lost. But wait — when env overrides with a positive value, the composed config drops `base.notes`. In `attachSpillWiring`, notes are printed from the composed `spills`. So a yaml section with a misconfigured `headChars: 10` (clamped with a note) would no longer print its note when FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD is also set. Minor, but a behavioral wrinkle: tolerant-parse notes silently swallowed by env override. Actually, notes would be useful to surface. Minor suggestion-level.

2. Also, `resolveRunSpillsConfig` with env set positive does NOT clamp `threshold`... fine, positive int.

3. `buildPreview` change: if body length <= headChars + tailChars, render body once. Note the boundary case: `body.length == headChars + tailChars` renders whole body; else head+tail with omitted marker. In the old code, a body of e.g. 3500 chars with head=2000/tail=2000: head=2000, tail=2000 — overlapping regions (head covers chars 0-2000, tail covers 1500-3500) → duplicated middle 500 chars and omitted = 3500-4000 = negative! So the old code had a real bug for bodies between head+tail/... hmm, actually the old bug fired when body.length < headChars + tailChars (omitted negative). The new code fixes it. Good fix. But is this a behavior change for legacy config (threshold 8192, head 2000, tail 2000)? A spilled body (> 8192 chars) always exceeds 4000, so the new branch only fires when threshold < head+tail, i.e. only under the env knob with small threshold, or a configured small threshold. So legacy behavior byte-identical for the default config. Good.

Wait — one more check: the "covered" branch does not codepoint-check; it renders the whole body, no cut, so no surrogate issue. OK.

All 25 new tests pass. Now let me continue the deep review. Remaining checks:

1. AGENTS.md conventions — check for env-var and export-list conventions.
2. Check `_effectiveCompactionSettings` consistency — the flutter_app parity test (`flutter_app/test/compaction_host_wiring_test.dart`) — does the app path need the bench knob too? The knob is CLI-only (documented). Check parity test still passes (settings semantics unchanged when env unset).
3. Check `resolveRunSpillsConfig` notes-drop wrinkle.
4. Check `benchCompactionTriggerTokens` — `int.tryParse` accepts leading `+`? `int.tryParse('+5')` = 5 in Dart. Fine.
5. Look at the `withCompactionTriggerTokens` doc "Two guards" listing three bullets — nit.
6. Check the interaction: `_effectiveCompactionSettings` with explicit `config.compactionSettings` override — env knob modifies it (contradicts PR description text "wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override"). Check the code comment again: "must win over both the defaults and a host default override". "host default override" = `resolveCompactionHostWiring` default? The PR description says "Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override." But the code applies the bench resolution unconditionally over `base` (which may be the explicit override). So the description is wrong OR the code is wrong. Which is intended? The doc comment in bench_trigger.dart and the code comment say it must win over both. The PR description contradicts. This is a doc/behavior mismatch worth an IMPORTANT or SUGGESTION. Since behavior: env knob overriding an explicit user config — for a bench run, the env is set by the bench harness intentionally; the machine operator sets both. Hmm, precedence question: user config file `compactionSettings` is an explicit user pin; env FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS is set by the bench harness (which is itself the user/automation). The PR description and code disagree — at minimum the description/comment mismatch is confusing. Let me determine the actual intent from tests: `agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` constructs AgentCliConfig WITHOUT compactionSettings, so no test covers env-vs-explicit-override. The code comment says "must win over both the defaults and a host default override" — the PR description says the opposite for explicit config. I'll flag as IMPORTANT (documented contract contradiction; add a test pinning the intended precedence).

Wait, actually let me re-read the PR description: "Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override." And the code: `resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...)` where base = override ?? wiring. Since the bench resolution is applied to `base` regardless, the env knob DOES override the explicit config (when trigger < window - override.reserveTokens). So PR description's "but not over an explicit config override" is FALSE per the code. The code comment says "must win over both the defaults and a host default override" — "a host default override" might mean the host-wiring defaults, not the user's explicit config.compactionSettings. So per the comment, does the knob win over `config.compactionSettings`? The comment is ambiguous. The behavior: yes it wins. The PR description: no it shouldn't. One of them is wrong. Flag it.

7. `agent_cli_spill.dart` — the `io.writeln('[spills] enabled via ...')` prints the raw env value. Value is an integer string; not a secret. OK. But note: it prints only when `config.spills == null` — when the env overrides an existing section's threshold, notice; minor.

8. `resolveRunSpillsConfig` drops section notes when env positive. The notes would have been printed by `attachSpillWiring` — losing them changes diagnostics under env runs. Minor suggestion.

9. `SpillsConfig(enabled: false)` for env `0`: `isActive` false → attach skipped. Good. But what if section=null and env=0? Returns disabled config instead of null — `attachSpillWiring` checks `spills != null && spills.isActive` → skip. Same outcome. OK.

10. The `buildPreview` early-return branch: header says `[spilled: N chars, L lines (threshold T chars)]` — good; body rendered whole; then `$spillReadHint` directly after body without a blank line? Let's compare: covered branch = `'$body\n' '$spillReadHint'` — no blank line between body and hint. Old shape: `'$tail\n' '$spillReadHint'` — also no blank line. Consistent. OK.

11. One more possible edge: `buildPreview` boundary `body.length <= headChars + tailChars` — at exactly head+tail, whole body once. Old behavior at exactly head+tail: head = headChars, tail = tailChars, omitted = 0 → `[... 0 chars omitted ...]` duplicated nothing (head+tail adjacent, no overlap, no negative marker) — so old rendered body once too plus a silly "[... 0 chars omitted ...]" marker. New: no marker. Better.

But hold on — the old code had a REAL bug for bodies in (max(head,tail), head+tail): duplicated overlapping region AND negative omitted count. Was that reachable pre-PR? Only when body.length <= head+tail AND body.length > threshold. Default threshold 8192 > 4000 → unreachable with defaults; reachable with a small configured threshold (e.g. threshold 3000, head/tail 2000 → body 3500: head 2000 + tail 2000 = 4000 > 3500 → duplicated 500 chars + omitted -500). So the bug was reachable pre-PR with custom config; the PR fixes it. Good — no compat concern since legacy default shapes are byte-identical.

12. `_codepointSafeSlice` vs spill's `_headExcerpt`: consistent rules. OK.

13. `shellJobCommandLabel` — single-line with flat.length in (head, head+tail]: returns full flat. The status line then carries up to 240 chars + the rest of the status line (id, state, age). The test bounds < 400. OK.

14. Multi-line command starting with '\n' or whitespace: firstLine empty → label " […N chars…]". Slight quality nit (leading space). Let me verify: command = "\nfoo bar" (multi-line? command.trim().contains('\n') — "\nfoo bar".trim() = "foo bar" no \n → single-line branch!). OK so for the multi-line branch, command.trim() contains '\n', but command.indexOf('\n') could still be 0 only if the command starts with '\n' AND trimmed contains '\n' — e.g. "\nfoo\nbar": trim() = "foo\nbar" contains \n → multi-line branch. firstLineEnd = indexOf('\n') = 0 → firstLine = "" → head = "" → label = " […7 chars…]". Leading space + empty face. Edge case, cosmetic. Worth a suggestion? Maybe fold into one suggestion about first-line extraction using the trimmed command.

15. The ticket AC2: "Replay of the jF7GNFh turn profile with the new caps: projected total input tokens ≤ ~3M (vs 11.2M)" — the PR explicitly says AC2's full turn-profile replay was not built; instead per-request bound asserted. This is a disclosed AC gap → flag in review as a note (IMPORTANT? The PR author disclosed it; the ticket AC is not fully satisfied). Per formatting_rules F10: "verify PR changes satisfy ticket ACs — note gaps in review". AC1 ✓ (fixture), AC2 partially (no replay; different assertion), AC3 ✓ (CLI test). I'll note AC2's substitution in the general comment and maybe as a SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT inline? It's a disclosed tradeoff, not a bug. General comment note.

16. Item 1 of the ticket's proposed fix: "drop stale done/lost cards from the rendered wall after they've been acknowledged (render only running + last K completed)" — the status wall ALREADY did running + last 20 (gh-1438). The settle notices are now one-shot per job. So the "supersede/compact registry snapshots in context" item: the settle notices are not superseded in context — each settle still adds ONE notice permanently to the transcript (bounded now, ~10x smaller). The accretion is bounded per job but still linear in job count (60 notices). The ticket wanted superseding; PR delivers bounding + relies on FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS to fold the accreted stream. Combined, that's a reasonable mechanism. Fine.

17. Security: no secrets involved; env knobs are numeric. The settle notice echoes the command — commands could contain secrets typed inline, but that was already the case; now LESS (bounded). Good.

18. Backward compat:…

Now the spill changes:

1. `resolveRunSpillsConfig` — env `0` → `const SpillsConfig(enabled: false)`. Note that the notes from a configured section are dropped when env wins (positive value): if the yaml section had notes (e.g., clamped bounds), those notes were printed in `attachSpillWiring` via `spills.notes`. When env overrides, notes from the section are lost. But wait — when env overrides with a positive value, the composed config drops `base.notes`. In `attachSpillWiring`, notes are printed from the composed `spills`. So a yaml section with a misconfigured `headChars: 10` (clamped with a note) would no longer print its note when FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD is also set. Minor, but a behavioral wrinkle: tolerant-parse notes silently swallowed by env override. Actually, notes would be useful to surface. Minor suggestion-level.

2. Also, `resolveRunSpillsConfig` with env set positive does NOT clamp `threshold`... fine, positive int.

3. `buildPreview` change: if body length <= headChars + tailChars, render body once. Note the boundary case: `body.length == headChars + tailChars` renders whole body; else head+tail with omitted marker. In the old code, a body of e.g. 3500 chars with head=2000/tail=2000: head=2000, tail=2000 — overlapping regions (head covers chars 0-2000, tail covers 1500-3500) → duplicated middle 500 chars and omitted = 3500-4000 = negative! So the old code had a real bug for bodies between head+tail/... hmm, actually the old bug fired when body.length < headChars + tailChars (omitted negative). The new code fixes it. Good fix. But is this a behavior change for legacy config (threshold 8192, head 2000, tail 2000)? A spilled body (> 8192 chars) always exceeds 4000, so the new branch only fires when threshold < head+tail, i.e. only under the env knob with small threshold, or a configured small threshold. So legacy behavior byte-identical for the default config. Good.

Wait — one more check: the "covered" branch does not codepoint-check; it renders the whole body, no cut, so no surrogate issue. OK.

4. `agent_cli_spill.dart`: the new log line prints `[spills] enabled via FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD=... (threshold N chars)`. Note: this only prints when `config.spills == null`. If config.spills != null and env overrides the threshold, note about the env override — minor.

blocks.text:
All 25 new tests pass. Now let me continue the deep review. Remaining checks:

1. AGENTS.md conventions — check for env-var and export-list conventions.
2. Check `_effectiveCompactionSettings` consistency — the flutter_app parity test (`flutter_app/test/compaction_host_wiring_test.dart`) — does the app path need the bench knob too? The knob is CLI-only (documented). Check parity test still passes (settings semantics unchanged when env unset).
3. Check `resolveRunSpillsConfig` notes-drop wrinkle.
4. Check `benchCompactionTriggerTokens` — `int.tryParse` accepts leading `+`? `int.tryParse('+5')` = 5 in Dart. Fine.
5. Look at the `withCompactionTriggerTokens` doc "Two guards" listing three bullets — nit.
6. Check the interaction: `_effectiveCompactionSettings` with explicit `config.compactionSettings` override — env knob modifies it (contradicts PR description text "wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override"). Check the code comment again: "must win over both the defaults and a host default override". "host default override" = `resolveCompactionHostWiring` default? The PR description says "Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override." But the code applies the bench resolution unconditionally over `base` (which may be the explicit override). So the description is wrong OR the code is wrong. Which is intended? The doc comment in bench_trigger.dart and the code comment say it must win over both. The PR description contradicts. This is a doc/behavior mismatch worth an IMPORTANT or SUGGESTION. Since behavior: env knob overriding an explicit user config — for a bench run, the env is set by the bench harness intentionally; the machine operator sets both. Hmm, precedence question: user config file `compactionSettings` is an explicit user pin; env FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS is set by the bench harness (which is itself the user/automation). The PR description and code disagree — at minimum the description/comment mismatch is confusing. Let me determine the actual intent from tests: `agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` constructs AgentCliConfig WITHOUT compactionSettings, so no test covers env-vs-explicit-override. The code comment says "must win over both the defaults and a host default override" — the PR description says the opposite for explicit config. I'll flag as IMPORTANT (documented contract contradiction; add a test pinning the intended precedence).

Wait, actually let me re-read the PR description: "Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override." And the code: `resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...)` where base = override ?? wiring. Since the bench resolution is applied to `base` regardless, the env knob DOES override the explicit config (when trigger < window - override.reserveTokens). So PR description's "but not over an explicit config override" is FALSE per the code. The code comment says "must win over both the defaults and a host default override" — "a host default override" might mean the host-wiring defaults, not the user's explicit config.compactionSettings. So per the comment, does the knob win over `config.compactionSettings`? The comment is ambiguous. The behavior: yes it wins. The PR description: no it shouldn't. One of them is wrong. Flag it.

7. `agent_cli_spill.dart` — the `io.writeln('[spills] enabled via ...')` prints the raw env value. Value is an integer string; not a secret. OK. But note: it prints only when `config.spills == null` — when the env overrides an existing section's threshold, notice; minor.

8. `resolveRunSpillsConfig` drops section notes when env positive. The notes would have been printed by `attachSpillWiring` — losing them changes diagnostics under env runs. Minor suggestion.

9. `SpillsConfig(enabled: false)` for env `0`: `isActive` false → attach skipped. Good. But what if section=null and env=0? Returns disabled config instead of null — `attachSpillWiring` checks `spills != null && spills.isActive` → skip. Same outcome. OK.

10. The `buildPreview` early-return branch: header says `[spilled: N chars, L lines (threshold T chars)]` — good; body rendered whole; then `$spillReadHint` directly after body without a blank line? Let's compare: covered branch = `'$body\n' '$spillReadHint'` — no blank line between body and hint. Old shape: `'$tail\n' '$spillReadHint'` — also no blank line. Consistent. OK.

11. One more possible edge: `buildPreview` boundary `body.length <= headChars + tailChars` — at exactly head+tail, whole body once. Old behavior at exactly head+tail: head = headChars, tail = tailChars, omitted = 0 → `[... 0 chars omitted ...]` duplicated nothing (head+tail adjacent, no overlap, no negative marker) — so old rendered body once too plus a silly "[... 0 chars omitted ...]" marker. New: no marker. Better.

But hold on — the old code had a REAL bug for bodies in (max(head,tail), head+tail): duplicated overlapping region AND negative omitted count. Was that reachable pre-PR? Only when body.length <= head+tail AND body.length > threshold. Default threshold 8192 > 4000 → unreachable with defaults; reachable with a small configured threshold (e.g. threshold 3000, head/tail 2000 → body 3500: head 2000 + tail 2000 = 4000 > 3500 → duplicated 500 chars + omitted -500). So the bug was reachable pre-PR with custom config; the PR fixes it. Good — no compat concern since legacy default shapes are byte-identical.

12. `_codepointSafeSlice` vs spill's `_headExcerpt`: consistent rules. OK.

13. `shellJobCommandLabel` — single-line with flat.length in (head, head+tail]: returns full flat. The status line then carries up to 240 chars + the rest of the status line (id, state, age). The test bounds < 400. OK.

14. Multi-line command starting with '\n' or whitespace: firstLine empty → label " […N chars…]". Slight quality nit (leading space). Let me verify: command = "\nfoo bar" (multi-line? command.trim().contains('\n') — "\nfoo bar".trim() = "foo bar" no \n → single-line branch!). OK so for the multi-line branch, command.trim() contains '\n', but command.indexOf('\n') could still be 0 only if the command starts with '\n' AND trimmed contains '\n' — e.g. "\nfoo\nbar": trim() = "foo\nbar" contains \n → multi-line branch. firstLineEnd = indexOf('\n') = 0 → firstLine = "" → head = "" → label = " […7 chars…]". Leading space + empty face. Edge case, cosmetic. Worth a suggestion? Maybe fold into one suggestion about first-line extraction using the trimmed command.

15. The ticket AC2: "Replay of the jF7GNFh turn profile with the new caps: projected total input tokens ≤ ~3M (vs 11.2M)" — the PR explicitly says AC2's full turn-profile replay was not built; instead per-request bound asserted. This is a disclosed AC gap → flag in review as a note (IMPORTANT? The PR author disclosed it; the ticket AC is not fully satisfied). Per formatting_rules F10: "verify PR changes satisfy ticket ACs — note gaps in review". AC1 ✓ (fixture), AC2 partially (no replay; different assertion), AC3 ✓ (CLI test). I'll note AC2's substitution in the general comment and maybe as a SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT inline? It's a disclosed tradeoff, not a bug. General comment note.

16. Item 1 of the ticket's proposed fix: "drop stale done/lost cards from the rendered wall after they've been acknowledged (render only running + last K completed)" — the status wall ALREADY did running + last 20 (gh-1438). The settle notices are now one-shot per job. So the "supersede/compact registry snapshots in context" item: the settle notices are not superseded in context — each settle still adds ONE notice permanently to the transcript (bounded now, ~10x smaller). The accretion is bounded per job but still linear in job count (60 notices). The ticket wanted superseding; PR delivers bounding + relies on FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS to fold the accreted stream. Combined, that's a reasonable mechanism. Fine.

17. Security: no secrets involved; env knobs are numeric. The settle notice echoes the command — commands could contain secrets typed inline, but that was already the case; now LESS (bounded). Good.

18. Backward compat:…

The doc comment in bench_trigger.dart and the code comment say it must win over both. The PR description contradicts. This is a doc/behavior mismatch worth an IMPORTANT or SUGGESTION. And the code: `resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...)` where base = override ?? wiring. Since the bench resolution is applied to `base` regardless, the env knob DOES override the explicit config (when trigger < window - override.reserveTokens). So PR description's "but not over an explicit config override" is FALSE per the code. The code comment says "must win over both the defaults and a host default override" — "a host default override" might mean the host-wiring defaults, not the user's explicit config.compactionSettings. 6. Check the interaction: `_effectiveCompactionSettings` with explicit `config.compactionSettings` override — env knob modifies it (contradicts PR description text "wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override"). Check the code comment again: "must win over both the defaults and a host default override". "host default override" = `resolveCompactionHostWiring` default? The PR description says "Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override." But the code applies the bench resolution unconditionally over `base` (which may be the explicit override). So the description is wrong OR the code is wrong. Which is intended? The doc comment in bench_trigger.dart and the code comment say it must win over both. The PR description contradicts. This is a doc/behavior mismatch worth an IMPORTANT or SUGGESTION. Since behavior: env knob overriding an explicit user config — for a bench run, the env is set by the bench harness intentionally; the machine operator sets both. Hmm, precedence question: user config file `compactionSettings` is an explicit user pin; env FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS is set by the bench harness (which is itself the user/automation). The PR description and code disagree — at minimum the description/comment mismatch is confusing. Let me determine the actual intent from tests: `agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` constructs AgentCliConfig WITHOUT compactionSettings, so no test covers env-vs-explicit-override. The code comment says "must win over both the defaults and a host default override" — the PR description says the opposite for explicit config. I'll flag as IMPORTANT (documented contract contradiction; add a test pinning the intended precedence).

Wait, actually let me re-read the PR description: "Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override." And the code: `resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...)` where base = override ?? wiring. Since the bench resolution is applied to `base` regardless, the env knob DOES override the explicit config (when trigger < window - override.reserveTokens). So PR description's "but not over an explicit config override" is FALSE per the code. The code comment says "must win over both the defaults and a host default override" — "a host default override" might mean the host-wiring defaults, not the user's explicit config.compactionSettings. So per the comment, does the knob win over `config.compactionSettings`? The comment is ambiguous. The behavior: yes it wins. The PR description: no it shouldn't. One of them is wrong. Flag it.

7. `agent_cli_spill.dart` — the `io.writeln('[spills] enabled via ...')` prints the raw env value. Value is an integer string; not a secret. OK. But note: it prints only when `config.spills == null` — when the env overrides an existing section's threshold, notice; minor.

8. `resolveRunSpillsConfig` drops section notes when env positive. The notes would have been printed by `attachSpillWiring` — losing them changes diagnostics under env runs. Minor suggestion.

9. `SpillsConfig(enabled: false)` for env `0`: `isActive` false → attach skipped. Good. But what if section=null and env=0? Returns disabled config instead of null — `attachSpillWiring` checks `spills != null && spills.isActive` → skip. Same outcome. OK.

10. The `buildPreview` early-return branch: header says `[spilled: N chars, L lines (threshold T chars)]` — good; body rendered whole; then `$spillReadHint` directly after body without a blank line? Let's compare: covered branch = `'$body\n' '$spillReadHint'` — no blank line between body and hint. Old shape: `'$tail\n' '$spillReadHint'` — also no blank line. Consistent. OK.

11. One more possible edge: `buildPreview` boundary `body.length <= headChars + tailChars` — at exactly head+tail, whole body once. Old behavior at exactly head+tail: head = headChars, tail = tailChars, omitted = 0 → `[... 0 chars omitted ...]` duplicated nothing (head+tail adjacent, no overlap, no negative marker) — so old rendered body once too plus a silly "[... 0 chars omitted ...]" marker. New: no marker. Better.

But hold on — the old code had a REAL bug for bodies in (max(head,tail), head+tail): duplicated overlapping region AND negative omitted count. Was that reachable pre-PR? Only when body.length <= head+tail AND body.length > threshold. Default threshold 8192 > 4000 → unreachable with defaults; reachable with a small configured threshold (e.g. threshold 3000, head/tail 2000 → body 3500: head 2000 + tail 2000 = 4000 > 3500 → duplicated 500 chars + omitted -500). So the bug was reachable pre-PR with custom config; the PR fixes it. Good — no compat concern since legacy default shapes are byte-identical.

OK so for the multi-line branch, command.trim() contains '\n', but command.indexOf('\n') could still be 0 only if the command starts with '\n' AND trimmed contains '\n' — e.g. "\nfoo\nbar": trim() = "foo\nbar" contains \n → multi-line branch. firstLineEnd = indexOf('\n') = 0 → firstLine = "" → head = "" → label = " […7 chars…]". Leading space + empty face. Edge case, cosmetic. Worth a suggestion? Maybe fold into one suggestion about first-line extraction using the trimmed command.

15. The ticket AC2: "Replay of the jF7GNFh turn profile with the new caps: projected total input tokens ≤ ~3M (vs 11.2M)" — the PR explicitly says AC2's full turn-profile replay was not built; instead per-request bound asserted. This is a disclosed AC gap → flag in review as a note (IMPORTANT? The PR author disclosed it; the ticket AC is not fully satisfied). I'll note AC2's substitution in the general comment and maybe as a SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT inline? It's a disclosed tradeoff, not a bug. General comment note.

Item 1 of the ticket's proposed fix: "drop stale done/lost cards from the rendered wall after they've been acknowledged (render only running + last K completed)" — the status wall ALREADY did running + last 20 (gh-1438). The settle notices are now one-shot per job. So the "supersede/compact registry snapshots in context" item: the settle notices are not superseded in context — each settle still adds ONE notice permanently to the transcript (bounded now, ~10x smaller). The accretion is bounded per job but still linear in job count (60 notices). The ticket wanted superseding; PR delivers bounding + relies on FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS to fold the accreted stream. Combined, that's a reasonable mechanism. Fine.

17. Security: no secrets involved; env knobs are numeric. The settle notice echoes the command — commands could contain secrets typed inline, but that was already the case; now LESS (bounded). Good.

blocks.text:
All 25 new tests pass. Now let me continue the deep review. Remaining checks:

1. AGENTS.md conventions — check for env-var and export-list conventions.
2. Check `_effectiveCompactionSettings` consistency — the flutter_app parity test (`flutter_app/test/compaction_host_wiring_test.dart`) — does the app path need the bench knob too? The knob is CLI-only (documented). Check parity test still passes (settings semantics unchanged when env unset).
3. Check `resolveRunSpillsConfig` notes-drop wrinkle.
4. Check `benchCompactionTriggerTokens` — `int.tryParse` accepts leading `+`? `int.tryParse('+5')` = 5 in Dart. Fine.
5. Look at the `withCompactionTriggerTokens` doc "Two guards" listing three bullets — nit.
6. Check the interaction: `_effectiveCompactionSettings` with explicit `config.compactionSettings` override — env knob modifies it (contradicts PR description text "wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override"). Check the code comment again: "must win over both the defaults and a host default override". "host default override" = `resolveCompactionHostWiring` default? The PR description says "Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override." But the code applies the bench resolution unconditionally over `base` (which may be the explicit override). So the description is wrong OR the code is wrong. Which is intended? The doc comment in bench_trigger.dart and the code comment say it must win over both. The PR description contradicts. This is a doc/behavior mismatch worth an IMPORTANT or SUGGESTION. Since behavior: env knob overriding an explicit user config — for a bench run, the env is set by the bench harness intentionally; the machine operator sets both. Hmm, precedence question: user config file `compactionSettings` is an explicit user pin; env FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS is set by the bench harness (which is itself the user/automation). The PR description and code disagree — at minimum the description/comment mismatch is confusing. Let me determine the actual intent from tests: `agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` constructs AgentCliConfig WITHOUT compactionSettings, so no test covers env-vs-explicit-override. The code comment says "must win over both the defaults and a host default override" — the PR description says the opposite for explicit config. I'll flag as IMPORTANT (documented contract contradiction; add a test pinning the intended precedence).

Wait, actually let me re-read the PR description: "Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override." And the code: `resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...)` where base = override ?? wiring. Since the bench resolution is applied to `base` regardless, the env knob DOES override the explicit config (when trigger < window - override.reserveTokens). So PR description's "but not over an explicit config override" is FALSE per the code. The code comment says "must win over both the defaults and a host default override" — "a host default override" might mean the host-wiring defaults, not the user's explicit config.compactionSettings. So per the comment, does the knob win over `config.compactionSettings`? The comment is ambiguous. The behavior: yes it wins. The PR description: no it shouldn't. One of them is wrong. Flag it.

7. `agent_cli_spill.dart` — the `io.writeln('[spills] enabled via ...')` prints the raw env value. Value is an integer string; not a secret. OK. But note: it prints only when `config.spills == null` — when the env overrides an existing section's threshold, notice; minor.

8. `resolveRunSpillsConfig` drops section notes when env positive. The notes would have been printed by `attachSpillWiring` — losing them changes diagnostics under env runs. Minor suggestion.

9. `SpillsConfig(enabled: false)` for env `0`: `isActive` false → attach skipped. Good. But what if section=null and env=0? Returns disabled config instead of null — `attachSpillWiring` checks `spills != null && spills.isActive` → skip. Same outcome. OK.

10. The `buildPreview` early-return branch: header says `[spilled: N chars, L lines (threshold T chars)]` — good; body rendered whole; then `$spillReadHint` directly after body without a blank line? Let's compare: covered branch = `'$body\n' '$spillReadHint'` — no blank line between body and hint. Old shape: `'$tail\n' '$spillReadHint'` — also no blank line. Consistent. OK.

11. One more possible edge: `buildPreview` boundary `body.length <= headChars + tailChars` — at exactly head+tail, whole body once. Old behavior at exactly head+tail: head = headChars, tail = tailChars, omitted = 0 → `[... 0 chars omitted ...]` duplicated nothing (head+tail adjacent, no overlap, no negative marker) — so old rendered body once too plus a silly "[... 0 chars omitted ...]" marker. New: no marker. Better.

But hold on — the old code had a REAL bug for bodies in (max(head,tail), head+tail): duplicated overlapping region AND negative omitted count. Was that reachable pre-PR? Only when body.length <= head+tail AND body.length > threshold. Default threshold 8192 > 4000 → unreachable with defaults; reachable with a small configured threshold (e.g. threshold 3000, head/tail 2000 → body 3500: head 2000 + tail 2000 = 4000 > 3500 → duplicated 500 chars + omitted -500). So the bug was reachable pre-PR with custom config; the PR fixes it. Good — no compat concern since legacy default shapes are byte-identical.

12. `_codepointSafeSlice` vs spill's `_headExcerpt`: consistent rules. OK.

13. `shellJobCommandLabel` — single-line with flat.length in (head, head+tail]: returns full flat. The status line then carries up to 240 chars + the rest of the status line (id, state, age). The test bounds < 400. OK.

14. Multi-line command starting with '\n' or whitespace: firstLine empty → label " […N chars…]". Slight quality nit (leading space). Let me verify: command = "\nfoo bar" (multi-line? command.trim().contains('\n') — "\nfoo bar".trim() = "foo bar" no \n → single-line branch!). OK so for the multi-line branch, command.trim() contains '\n', but command.indexOf('\n') could still be 0 only if the command starts with '\n' AND trimmed contains '\n' — e.g. "\nfoo\nbar": trim() = "foo\nbar" contains \n → multi-line branch. firstLineEnd = indexOf('\n') = 0 → firstLine = "" → head = "" → label = " […7 chars…]". Leading space + empty face. Edge case, cosmetic. Worth a suggestion? Maybe fold into one suggestion about first-line extraction using the trimmed command.

15. The ticket AC2: "Replay of the jF7GNFh turn profile with the new caps: projected total input tokens ≤ ~3M (vs 11.2M)" — the PR explicitly says AC2's full turn-profile replay was not built; instead per-request bound asserted. This is a disclosed AC gap → flag in review as a note (IMPORTANT? The PR author disclosed it; the ticket AC is not fully satisfied). Per formatting_rules F10: "verify PR changes satisfy ticket ACs — note gaps in review". AC1 ✓ (fixture), AC2 partially (no replay; different assertion), AC3 ✓ (CLI test). I'll note AC2's substitution in the general comment and maybe as a SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT inline? It's a disclosed tradeoff, not a bug. General comment note.

16. Item 1 of the ticket's proposed fix: "drop stale done/lost cards from the rendered wall after they've been acknowledged (render only running + last K completed)" — the status wall ALREADY did running + last 20 (gh-1438). The settle notices are now one-shot per job. So the "supersede/compact registry snapshots in context" item: the settle notices are not superseded in context — each settle still adds ONE notice permanently to the transcript (bounded now, ~10x smaller). The accretion is bounded per job but still linear in job count (60 notices). The ticket wanted superseding; PR delivers bounding + relies on FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS to fold the accreted stream. Combined, that's a reasonable mechanism. Fine.

17. Security: no secrets involved; env knobs are numeric. The settle notice echoes the command — commands could contain secrets typed inline, but that was already the case; now LESS (bounded). Good.

18. Backward compat:…

blocks.text:
Confirmed: `200.clamp(1, 0)` throws ArgumentError in Dart. So:

`FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS=1` → `benchCompactionTriggerTokens` returns 1 (valid positive integer). → `withCompactionTriggerTokens`: clamped = 1; `clamped ~/ 2` = 0; `base.keepRecentTokens.clamp(1, 0)` → **ArgumentError thrown**.

Where does it propagate? `_effectiveCompactionSettings` is called in:
- `_autoCompactGate`-ish paths (`shouldCompact(tokens, _effectiveContextWindow, _effectiveCompactionSettings)`) — on every turn boundary check
- `session_commands.dart:606` (`/compact` command)
- The boot cap (`_capResumedContext`)

So setting `FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS=1` (or any value that yields `clamped ~/ 2 == 0`, i.e. clamped < 2 → clamped = 1 only since clamp lower bound is 1) crashes the compaction gate → likely breaks the run/boot. Let me confirm the propagation is uncaught: `shouldCompact(tokens, _effectiveContextWindow, _effectiveCompactionSettings)` — if the getter throws inside `_capResumedContext`'s try? No — the throw happens BEFORE the try block (the `shouldCompact` call at line ~347 is outside try). In `_capResumedContext`, the `shouldCompact` call is also before `_pushBusyPhase`. So an ArgumentError propagates up through boot → run dies.

Is trigger=1 realistic? A bench harness misconfiguration (FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS=1, or 0-string? no, 0 → null). Values 1..(2*keepRecent? no): the throw happens iff `clamped ~/ 2 < 1`, i.e. clamped < 2, i.e. clamped == 1. Only triggerTokens=1 (or negative→clamped to 1! wait: clamp(1, window) — a NEGATIVE env is rejected by the parse (parsed > 0 required). But what about triggerTokens values between 1 and window? clamped = trigger.clamp(1, window) — trigger >= 1 after parse. So clamped=1 only when trigger=1. So the crash needs exactly FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS=1. Pathological but a real unguarded crash — the doc explicitly promises "junk never breaks a boot — the default behavior applies" and the guards are supposed to keep the pass "sane". A one-character env value bricks the run with an ArgumentError instead of falling back. That's a genuine correctness bug (BLOCKING? It requires an operator setting the env to exactly "1" — an edge misconfiguration. The blast radius: bench harness crashes at boot instead of compacting). Severity: the mandate says BLOCKING = "merge would cause a bug... Must be fixed". This is a latent crash reachable through the new public API with a documented valid input. I'd rate it IMPORTANT (edge-case input crashes a knob meant to be robust; fix is one line: `max(1, clamped ~/ 2)` or guard `clamped < 2 → keep 1`). Hmm. The value "1" is nonsense but the parse contract says positive integers are honored, and the doc claims guards keep everything sane. A crash in a getter used by the run loop = broken behavior under valid input. I'll classify BLOCKING? Let me think about the harness's own conventions: env junk never breaks a boot; but "1" is not junk by their own parse rules. The failure mode is a hard ArgumentError at boot/run — data loss no, security no, but broken behavior for a supported input. The verdict rules: BLOCKING = correctness/bug findings: broken behavior. Given the input is valid per the documented contract and the crash aborts the run, I lean IMPORTANT-to-BLOCKING. The actual likelihood: a bench operator typing "1" — unlikely; but "0"? rejected (parsed > 0 → null → default). Only literal "1". Honestly this is an edge robustness bug → I'll mark BLOCKING? Let me re-read severity defs: "BLOCKING — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed." A reachable crash from a documented-valid input IS a bug the merge introduces. But proportionality: the machine treats BLOCKING as rework-required. A one-line fix; the rework cost is justified vs shipping a latent crash. Hmm — but verdict rules also warn against over-blocking on nits. A crash reachable only via triggerTokens==1 (absurd config)... I'll classify as IMPORTANT with a clear repro (the clamp contract violation is real and the fix is trivial), since it requires a nonsensical-but-technically-valid value and does not affect any realistic run. Hmm, "When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible." Risk of an operator setting =1: negligible? The env var's documented domain is "an ABSOLUTE context size" like 600–800. =1 is a typo-class value (e.g. "1" instead of "1000"... eh). A crash-on-typo for a boot env knob in an UNATTENDED bench run means the whole bench run dies with a confusing ArgumentError. I'll go BLOCKING with the one-line fix — it's a genuine correctness defect reachable through the public API with valid input, and the whole PR's selling point is "junk never breaks a boot". Actually wait — let me double-check the claim "junk never breaks a boot" applies only to parse-level junk. The docstring: "(junk never breaks a boot — the default behavior applies)" — refers to non-integer strings. For integer 1, no guard exists. The `withCompactionTriggerTokens` doc says "Two guards keep the pass sane" — and the guards are about budget, not crash-safety. So the contract gap is real but narrow.

Decision: BLOCKING is defensible; but let me weigh the machine protocol — a rework round costs 15-20 CI minutes. The fix is trivial and clearly worth it (a crash in the run loop). I'll mark it BLOCKING (correctness: uncaught ArgumentError from a valid env value bricks every gate that reads the getter). Per the verdict mapping, BLOCKING → REQUEST_CHANGES. Hmm, let me also weigh: is there a second real blocking/important finding to bundle so the rework round is worthwhile? Let me list all findings first, then decide.

blocks.text:
Confirmed: `200.clamp(1, 0)` throws ArgumentError in Dart. So:

`FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS=1` → `benchCompactionTriggerTokens` returns 1 (valid positive integer). → `withCompactionTriggerTokens`: clamped = 1; `clamped ~/ 2` = 0; `base.keepRecentTokens.clamp(1, 0)` → **ArgumentError thrown**.

Where does it propagate? `_effectiveCompactionSettings` is called in:
- `_autoCompactGate`-ish paths (`shouldCompact(tokens, _effectiveContextWindow, _effectiveCompactionSettings)`) — on every turn boundary check
- `session_commands.dart:606` (`/compact` command)
- The boot cap (`_capResumedContext`)

So setting `FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS=1` (or any value that yields `clamped ~/ 2 == 0`, i.e. clamped < 2 → clamped = 1 only since clamp lower bound is 1) crashes the compaction gate → likely breaks the run/boot. All 25 new tests pass. Now let me continue the deep review. Remaining checks:

1. AGENTS.md conventions — check for env-var and export-list conventions.
2. Check `_effectiveCompactionSettings` consistency — the flutter_app parity test (`flutter_app/test/compaction_host_wiring_test.dart`) — does the app path need the bench knob too? The knob is CLI-only (documented). Check parity test still passes (settings semantics unchanged when env unset).
3. Check `resolveRunSpillsConfig` notes-drop wrinkle.
4. Check `benchCompactionTriggerTokens` — `int.tryParse` accepts leading `+`? `int.tryParse('+5')` = 5 in Dart. Fine.
5. Look at the `withCompactionTriggerTokens` doc "Two guards" listing three bullets — nit.
6. Check the interaction: `_effectiveCompactionSettings` with explicit `config.compactionSettings` override — env knob modifies it (contradicts PR description text "wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override"). Check the code comment again: "must win over both the defaults and a host default override". "host default override" = `resolveCompactionHostWiring` default? The PR description says "Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override." But the code applies the bench resolution unconditionally over `base` (which may be the explicit override). So the description is wrong OR the code is wrong. Which is intended? The doc comment in bench_trigger.dart and the code comment say it must win over both. The PR description contradicts. This is a doc/behavior mismatch worth an IMPORTANT or SUGGESTION. Since behavior: env knob overriding an explicit user config — for a bench run, the env is set by the bench harness intentionally; the machine operator sets both. Hmm, precedence question: user config file `compactionSettings` is an explicit user pin; env FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS is set by the bench harness (which is itself the user/automation). The PR description and code disagree — at minimum the description/comment mismatch is confusing. Let me determine the actual intent from tests: `agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` constructs AgentCliConfig WITHOUT compactionSettings, so no test covers env-vs-explicit-override. The code comment says "must win over both the defaults and a host default override" — the PR description says the opposite for explicit config. I'll flag as IMPORTANT (documented contract contradiction; add a test pinning the intended precedence).

Wait, actually let me re-read the PR description: "Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override." And the code: `resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...)` where base = override ?? wiring. Since the bench resolution is applied to `base` regardless, the env knob DOES override the explicit config (when trigger < window - override.reserveTokens). So PR description's "but not over an explicit config override" is FALSE per the code. The code comment says "must win over both the defaults and a host default override" — "a host default override" might mean the host-wiring defaults, not the user's explicit config.compactionSettings. So per the comment, does the knob win over `config.compactionSettings`? The comment is ambiguous. The behavior: yes it wins. The PR description: no it shouldn't. One of them is wrong. Flag it.

7. `agent_cli_spill.dart` — the `io.writeln('[spills] enabled via ...')` prints the raw env value. Value is an integer string; not a secret. OK. But note: it prints only when `config.spills == null` — when the env overrides an existing section's threshold, notice; minor.

8. `resolveRunSpillsConfig` drops section notes when env positive. The notes would have been printed by `attachSpillWiring` — losing them changes diagnostics under env runs. Minor suggestion.

9. `SpillsConfig(enabled: false)` for env `0`: `isActive` false → attach skipped. Good. But what if section=null and env=0? Returns disabled config instead of null — `attachSpillWiring` checks `spills != null && spills.isActive` → skip. Same outcome. OK.

10. The `buildPreview` early-return branch: header says `[spilled: N chars, L lines (threshold T chars)]` — good; body rendered whole; then `$spillReadHint` directly after body without a blank line? Let's compare: covered branch = `'$body\n' '$spillReadHint'` — no blank line between body and hint. Old shape: `'$tail\n' '$spillReadHint'` — also no blank line. Consistent. OK.

11. One more possible edge: `buildPreview` boundary `body.length <= headChars + tailChars` — at exactly head+tail, whole body once. Old behavior at exactly head+tail: head = headChars, tail = tailChars, omitted = 0 → `[... 0 chars omitted ...]` duplicated nothing (head+tail adjacent, no overlap, no negative marker) — so old rendered body once too plus a silly "[... 0 chars omitted ...]" marker. New: no marker. Better.

But hold on — the old code had a REAL bug for bodies in (max(head,tail), head+tail): duplicated overlapping region AND negative omitted count. Was that reachable pre-PR? Only when body.length <= head+tail AND body.length > threshold. Default threshold 8192 > 4000 → unreachable with defaults; reachable with a small configured threshold (e.g. threshold 3000, head/tail 2000 → body 3500: head 2000 + tail 2000 = 4000 > 3500 → duplicated 500 chars + omitted -500). So the bug was reachable pre-PR with custom config; the PR fixes it. Good — no compat concern since legacy default shapes are byte-identical.

12. `_codepointSafeSlice` vs spill's `_headExcerpt`: consistent rules. OK.

13. `shellJobCommandLabel` — single-line with flat.length in (head, head+tail]: returns full flat. The status line then carries up to 240 chars + the rest of the status line (id, state, age). The test bounds < 400. OK.

14. Multi-line command starting with '\n' or whitespace: firstLine empty → label " […N chars…]". Slight quality nit (leading space). Let me verify: command = "\nfoo bar" (multi-line? command.trim().contains('\n') — "\nfoo bar".trim() = "foo bar" no \n → single-line branch!). OK so for the multi-line branch, command.trim() contains '\n', but command.indexOf('\n') could still be 0 only if the command starts with '\n' AND trimmed contains '\n' — e.g. "\nfoo\nbar": trim() = "foo\nbar" contains \n → multi-line branch. firstLineEnd = indexOf('\n') = 0 → firstLine = "" → head = "" → label = " […7 chars…]". Leading space + empty face. Edge case, cosmetic. Worth a suggestion? Maybe fold into one suggestion about first-line extraction using the trimmed command.

15. The ticket AC2: "Replay of the jF7GNFh turn profile with the new caps: projected total input tokens ≤ ~3M (vs 11.2M)" — the PR explicitly says AC2's full turn-profile replay was not built; instead per-request bound asserted. This is a disclosed AC gap → flag in review as a note (IMPORTANT? The PR author disclosed it; the ticket AC is not fully satisfied). Per formatting_rules F10: "verify PR changes satisfy ticket ACs — note gaps in review". AC1 ✓ (fixture), AC2 partially (no replay; different assertion), AC3 ✓ (CLI test). I'll note AC2's substitution in the general comment and maybe as a SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT inline? It's a disclosed tradeoff, not a bug. General comment note.

Item 1 of the ticket's proposed fix: "drop stale done/lost cards from the rendered wall after they've been acknowledged (render only running + last K completed)" — the status wall ALREADY did running + last 20 (gh-1438). The settle notices are now one-shot per job. So the "supersede/compact registry snapshots in context" item: the settle notices are not superseded in context — each settle still adds ONE notice permanently to the transcript (bounded now, ~10x smaller). The accretion is bounded per job but still linear in job count (60 notices). The ticket wanted superseding; PR delivers bounding + relies on FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS to fold the accreted stream. Combined, that's a reasonable mechanism. Fine.

17. Security: no secrets involved; env knobs are numeric. The settle notice echoes the command — commands could contain secrets typed inline, but that was already the case; now LESS (bounded). Good.

Confirmed: `200.clamp(1, 0)` throws ArgumentError in Dart. So:

`FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS=1` → `benchCompactionTriggerTokens` returns 1 (valid positive integer). → `withCompactionTriggerTokens`: clamped = 1; `clamped ~/ 2` = 0; `base.keepRecentTokens.clamp(1, 0)` → **ArgumentError thrown**.

Where does it propagate? `_effectiveCompactionSettings` is called in:
- `_autoCompactGate`-ish paths (`shouldCompact(tokens, _effectiveContextWindow, _effectiveCompactionSettings)`) — on every turn boundary check
- `session_commands.dart:606` (`/compact` command)
- The boot cap (`_capResumedContext`)

So setting `FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS=1` (or any value that yields `clamped ~/ 2 == 0`, i.e. clamped < 2 → clamped = 1 only since clamp lower bound is 1) crashes the compaction gate → likely breaks the run/boot. Let me confirm the propagation is uncaught: `shouldCompact(tokens, _effectiveContextWindow, _effectiveCompactionSettings)` — if the getter throws inside `_capResumedContext`'s try? No — the throw happens BEFORE the try block (the `shouldCompact` call at line ~347 is outside try). In `_capResumedContext`, the `shouldCompact` call is also before `_pushBusyPhase`. So an ArgumentError propagates up through boot → run dies.

Is trigger=1 realistic? A bench harness misconfiguration (FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS=1, or 0-string? no, 0 → null). Values 1..(2*keepRecent? no): the throw happens iff `clamped ~/ 2 < 1`, i.e. clamped < 2, i.e. clamped == 1. Only triggerTokens=1 (or negative→clamped to 1! wait: clamp(1, window) — a NEGATIVE env is rejected by the parse (parsed > 0 required). But what about triggerTokens values between 1 and window? clamped = trigger.clamp(1, window) — trigger >= 1 after parse. So clamped=1 only when trigger=1. So the crash needs exactly FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS=1. Pathological but a real unguarded crash — the doc explicitly promises "junk never breaks a boot — the default behavior applies" and the guards are supposed to keep the pass "sane". A one-character env value bricks the run with an ArgumentError instead of falling back. That's a genuine correctness bug (BLOCKING? It requires an operator setting the env to exactly "1" — an edge misconfiguration. The blast radius: bench harness crashes at boot instead of compacting). Severity: the mandate says BLOCKING = "merge would cause a bug... Must be fixed". This is a latent crash reachable through the new public API with a documented valid input. I'd rate it IMPORTANT (edge-case input crashes a knob meant to be robust; fix is one line: `max(1, clamped ~/ 2)` or guard `clamped < 2 → keep 1`). Hmm. The value "1" is nonsense but the parse contract says positive integers are honored, and the doc claims guards keep everything sane. A crash in a getter used by the run loop = broken behavior under valid input. I'll classify BLOCKING? Let me think about the harness's own conventions: env junk never breaks a boot; but "1" is not junk by their own parse rules. Check the code comment again: "must win over both the defaults and a host default override". "host default override" = `resolveCompactionHostWiring` default? The PR description says "Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override." But the code applies the bench resolution unconditionally over `base` (which may be the explicit override). So the description is wrong OR the code is wrong. Which is intended? The doc comment in bench_trigger.dart and the code comment say it must win over both. The PR description contradicts. This is a doc/behavior mismatch worth an IMPORTANT or SUGGESTION. Since behavior: env knob overriding an explicit user config — for a bench run, the env is set by the bench harness intentionally; the machine operator sets both. Hmm, precedence question: user config file `compactionSettings` is an explicit user pin; env FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS is set by the bench harness (which is itself the user/automation). The PR description and code disagree — at minimum the description/comment mismatch is confusing. Let me determine the actual intent from tests: `agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` constructs AgentCliConfig WITHOUT compactionSettings, so no test covers env-vs-explicit-override. The code comment says "must win over both the defaults and a host default override" — the PR description says the opposite for explicit config. I'll flag as IMPORTANT (documented contract contradiction; add a test pinning the intended precedence).

Wait, actually let me re-read the PR description: "Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override." And the code: `resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...)` where base = override ?? wiring. Since the bench resolution is applied to `base` regardless, the env knob DOES override the explicit config (when trigger < window - override.reserveTokens). So PR description's "but not over an explicit config override" is FALSE per the code. The code comment says "must win over both the defaults and a host default override" — "a host default override" might mean the host-wiring defaults, not the user's explicit config.compactionSettings. So per the comment, does the knob win over `config.compactionSettings`? The comment is ambiguous. The behavior: yes it wins. The PR description: no it shouldn't. One of them is wrong. Flag it.

Let's compare: covered branch = `'$body\n' '$spillReadHint'` — no blank line between body and hint. Old shape: `'$tail\n' '$spillReadHint'` — also no blank line. Consistent. OK.

Check the interaction: `_effectiveCompactionSettings` with explicit `config.compactionSettings` override — env knob modifies it (contradicts PR description text "wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override"). Check the code comment again: "must win over both the defaults and a host default override". "host default override" = `resolveCompactionHostWiring` default? The PR description says "Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override." But the code applies the bench resolution unconditionally over `base` (which may be the explicit override). So the description is wrong OR the code is wrong. Which is intended? The doc comment in bench_trigger.dart and the code comment say it must win over both. The PR description contradicts. This is a doc/behavior mismatch worth an IMPORTANT or SUGGESTION. Since behavior: env knob overriding an explicit user config — for a bench run, the env is set by the bench harness intentionally; the machine operator sets both. Hmm, precedence question: user config file `compactionSettings` is an explicit user pin; env FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS is set by the bench harness (which is itself the user/automation). The PR description and code disagree — at minimum the description/comment mismatch is confusing. Let me determine the actual intent from tests: `agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` constructs AgentCliConfig WITHOUT compactionSettings, so no test covers env-vs-explicit-override. The code comment says "must win over both the defaults and a host default override" — the PR description says the opposite for explicit config. I'll flag as IMPORTANT (documented contract contradiction; add a test pinning the intended precedence).

Wait, actually let me re-read the PR description: "Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override." And the code: `resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...)` where base = override ?? wiring. Since the bench resolution is applied to `base` regardless, the env knob DOES override the explicit config (when trigger < window - override.reserveTokens). So PR description's "but not over an explicit config override" is FALSE per the code. The code comment says "must win over both the defaults and a host default override" — "a host default override" might mean the host-wiring defaults, not the user's explicit config.compactionSettings. So per the comment, does the knob win over `config.compactionSettings`? The comment is ambiguous. The behavior: yes it wins. The PR description: no it shouldn't. One of them is wrong. Flag it.

7. `agent_cli_spill.dart` — the `io.writeln('[spills] enabled via ...')` prints the raw env value. Value is an integer string; not a secret. OK. But note: it prints only when `config.spills == null` — when the env overrides an existing section's threshold, notice; minor.

8. `resolveRunSpillsConfig` drops section notes when env positive. The notes would have been printed by `attachSpillWiring` — losing them changes diagnostics under env runs. Minor suggestion.

9. `SpillsConfig(enabled: false)` for env `0`: `isActive` false → attach skipped. Good. But what if section=null and env=0? Returns disabled config instead of null — `attachSpillWiring` checks `spills != null && spills.isActive` → skip. Same outcome. OK.

10. The `buildPreview` early-return branch: header says `[spilled: N chars, L lines (threshold T chars)]` — good; body rendered whole; then `$spillReadHint` directly after body without a blank line? Let's compare: covered branch = `'$body\n' '$spillReadHint'` — no blank line between body and hint. Old shape: `'$tail\n' '$spillReadHint'` — also no blank line. Consistent. OK.

11. One more possible edge: `buildPreview` boundary `body.length <= headChars + tailChars` — at exactly head+tail, whole body once. Old behavior at exactly head+tail: head = headChars, tail = tailChars, omitted = 0 → `[... 0 chars omitted ...]` duplicated nothing (head+tail adjacent, no overlap, no negative marker) — so old rendered body once too plus a silly "[... 0 chars omitted ...]" marker. New: no marker. Better.

But hold on — the old code had a REAL bug for bodies in (max(head,tail), head+tail): duplicated overlapping region AND negative omitted count. Was that reachable pre-PR? Only when body.length <= head+tail AND body.length > threshold. Default threshold 8192 > 4000 → unreachable with defaults; reachable with a small configured threshold (e.g. threshold 3000, head/tail 2000 → body 3500: head 2000 + tail 2000 = 4000 > 3500 → duplicated 500 chars + omitted -500).
