The PR description says "Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override." But the code applies the bench resolution unconditionally over `base` (which may be the explicit override). So the description is wrong OR the code is wrong. Which is intended? The doc comment in bench_trigger.dart and the code comment say it must win over both. The PR description contradicts. This is a doc/behavior mismatch worth an IMPORTANT or SUGGESTION. Since behavior: env knob overriding an explicit user config — for a bench run, the env is set by the bench harness intentionally; the machine operator sets both. The code comment says "must win over both the defaults and a host default override" — the PR description says the opposite for explicit config. Wait, actually let me re-read the PR description: "Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override." And the code: `resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...)` where base = override ?? wiring. Since the bench resolution is applied to `base` regardless, the env knob DOES override the explicit config (when trigger < window - override.reserveTokens). So PR description's "but not over an explicit config override" is FALSE per the code. The code comment says "must win over both the defaults and a host default override" — "a host default override" might mean the host-wiring defaults, not the user's explicit config.compactionSettings. The PR description says "Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override." But the code applies the bench resolution unconditionally over `base` (which may be the explicit override). So the description is wrong OR the code is wrong. Which is intended? The doc comment in bench_trigger.dart and the code comment say it must win over both. The PR description contradicts. This is a doc/behavior mismatch worth an IMPORTANT or SUGGESTION. Since behavior: env knob overriding an explicit user config — for a bench run, the env is set by the bench harness intentionally; the machine operator sets both. Hmm, precedence question: user config file `compactionSettings` is an explicit user pin; env FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS is set by the bench harness (which is itself the user/automation). The PR description and code disagree — at minimum the description/comment mismatch is confusing. Let me determine the actual intent from tests: `agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` constructs AgentCliConfig WITHOUT compactionSettings, so no test covers env-vs-explicit-override. The code comment says "must win over both the defaults and a host default override" — the PR description says the opposite for explicit config. I'll flag as IMPORTANT (documented contract contradiction; add a test pinning the intended precedence).

Wait, actually let me re-read the PR description: "Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override." And the code: `resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...)` where base = override ?? wiring. Since the bench resolution is applied to `base` regardless, the env knob DOES override the explicit config (when trigger < window - override.reserveTokens). So PR description's "but not over an explicit config override" is FALSE per the code. The code comment says "must win over both the defaults and a host default override" — "a host default override" might mean the host-wiring defaults, not the user's explicit config.compactionSettings. So per the comment, does the knob win over `config.compactionSettings`? The comment is ambiguous. The behavior: yes it wins. The PR description: no it shouldn't. One of them is wrong. Flag it.

7. `agent_cli_spill.dart` — the `io.writeln('[spills] enabled via ...')` prints the raw env value. Value is an integer string; not a secret. OK. But note: it prints only when `config.spills == null` — when the env overrides an existing section's threshold, notice; minor.

8. `resolveRunSpillsConfig` drops section notes when env positive. The notes would have been printed by `attachSpillWiring` — losing them changes diagnostics under env runs. Minor suggestion.

9. `SpillsConfig(enabled: false)` for env `0`: `isActive` false → attach skipped. Good. But what if section=null and env=0? Returns disabled config instead of null — `attachSpillWiring` checks `spills != null && spills.isActive` → skip. Same outcome. OK.

10. The `buildPreview` early-return branch: header says `[spilled: N chars, L lines (threshold T chars)]` — good; body rendered whole; then `$spillReadHint` directly after body without a blank line? Let's compare: covered branch = `'$body\n' '$spillReadHint'` — no blank line between body and hint. Old shape: `'$tail\n' '$spillReadHint'` — also no blank line. Consistent. OK.

11. One more possible edge: `buildPreview` boundary `body.length <= headChars + tailChars` — at exactly head+tail, whole body once. Old behavior at exactly head+tail: head = headChars, tail = tailChars, omitted = 0 → `[... 0 chars omitted ...]` duplicated nothing (head+tail adjacent, no overlap, no negative marker) — so old rendered body once too plus a silly "[... 0 chars omitted ...]" marker. New: no marker. Better.

But hold on — the old code had a REAL bug for bodies in (max(head,tail), head+tail): duplicated overlapping region AND negative omitted count. Was that reachable pre-PR? Only when body.length <= head+tail AND body.length > threshold. Default threshold 8192 > 4000 → unreachable with defaults; reachable with a small configured threshold (e.g. threshold 3000, head/tail 2000 → body 3500: head 2000 + tail 2000 = 4000 > 3500 → duplicated 500 chars + omitted -500). So the bug was reachable pre-PR with custom config; the PR fixes it. Good — no compat concern since legacy default shapes are byte-identical.

12. `_codepointSafeSlice` vs spill's `_headExcerpt`: consistent rules. OK.

13. `shellJobCommandLabel` — single-line with flat.length in (head, head+tail]: returns full flat. The status line then carries up to 240 chars + the rest of the status line (id, state, age). The test bounds < 400. OK.

14. Multi-line command starting with '\n' or whitespace: firstLine empty → label " […N chars…]". Slight quality nit (leading space). Let me verify: command = "\nfoo bar" (multi-line? command.trim().contains('\n') — "\nfoo bar".trim() = "foo bar" no \n → single-line branch!). OK so for the multi-line branch, command.trim() contains '\n', but command.indexOf('\n') could still be 0 only if the command starts with '\n' AND trimmed contains '\n' — e.g. "\nfoo\nbar": trim() = "foo\nbar" contains \n → multi-line branch. firstLineEnd = indexOf('\n') = 0 → firstLine = "" → head = "" → label = " […7 chars…]". Leading space + empty face. Edge case, cosmetic. Worth a suggestion? Maybe fold into one suggestion about first-line extraction using the trimmed command.

15. The ticket AC2: "Replay of the jF7GNFh turn profile with the new caps: projected total input tokens ≤ ~3M (vs 11.2M)" — the PR explicitly says AC2's full turn-profile replay was not built; instead per-request bound asserted. This is a disclosed AC gap → flag in review as a note (IMPORTANT? The PR author disclosed it; the ticket AC is not fully satisfied). Per formatting_rules F10: "verify PR changes satisfy ticket ACs — note gaps in review". AC1 ✓ (fixture), AC2 partially (no replay; different assertion), AC3 ✓ (CLI test). I'll note AC2's substitution in the general comment and maybe as a SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT inline? It's a disclosed tradeoff, not a bug. General comment note.

16. Item 1 of the ticket's proposed fix: "drop stale done/lost cards from the rendered wall after they've been acknowledged (render only running + last K completed)" — the status wall ALREADY did running + last 20 (gh-1438). The settle notices are now one-shot per job. So the "supersede/compact registry snapshots in context" item: the settle notices are not superseded in context — each settle still adds ONE notice permanently to the transcript (bounded now, ~10x smaller). The accretion is bounded per job but still linear in job count (60 notices). The ticket wanted superseding; PR delivers bounding + relies on FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS to fold the accreted stream. Combined, that's a reasonable mechanism. Fine.

17. Security: no secrets involved; env knobs are numeric. The settle notice echoes the command — commands could contain secrets typed inline, but that was already the case; now LESS (bounded). Good.

Check the interaction: `_effectiveCompactionSettings` with explicit `config.compactionSettings` override — env knob modifies it (contradicts PR description text "wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override"). Check the code comment again: "must win over both the defaults and a host default override". "host default override" = `resolveCompactionHostWiring` default? The PR description says "Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override." But the code applies the bench resolution unconditionally over `base` (which may be the explicit override). So the description is wrong OR the code is wrong. Which is intended? The doc comment in bench_trigger.dart and the code comment say it must win over both. The PR description contradicts. This is a doc/behavior mismatch worth an IMPORTANT or SUGGESTION. Since behavior: env knob overriding an explicit user config — for a bench run, the env is set by the bench harness intentionally; the machine operator sets both. Hmm, precedence question: user config file `compactionSettings` is an explicit user pin; env FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS is set by the bench harness (which is itself the user/automation). The PR description and code disagree — at minimum the description/comment mismatch is confusing. Let me determine the actual intent from tests: `agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` constructs AgentCliConfig WITHOUT compactionSettings, so no test covers env-vs-explicit-override. The code comment says "must win over both the defaults and a host default override" — the PR description says the opposite for explicit config. I'll flag as IMPORTANT (documented contract contradiction; add a test pinning the intended precedence).

Wait, actually let me re-read the PR description: "Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override." And the code: `resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...)` where base = override ?? wiring. Since the bench resolution is applied to `base` regardless, the env knob DOES override the explicit config (when trigger < window - override.reserveTokens). So PR description's "but not over an explicit config override" is FALSE per the code. The code comment says "must win over both the defaults and a host default override" — "a host default override" might mean the host-wiring defaults, not the user's explicit config.compactionSettings. So per the comment, does the knob win over `config.compactionSettings`? The comment is ambiguous. The behavior: yes it wins. The PR description: no it shouldn't. One of them is wrong. Flag it.

7. `agent_cli_spill.dart` — the `io.writeln('[spills] enabled via ...')` prints the raw env value. Value is an integer string; not a secret. OK. But note: it prints only when `config.spills == null` — when the env overrides an existing section's threshold, notice; minor.

8. `resolveRunSpillsConfig` drops section notes when env positive. The notes would have been printed by `attachSpillWiring` — losing them changes diagnostics under env runs. Minor suggestion.

9. `SpillsConfig(enabled: false)` for env `0`: `isActive` false → attach skipped. Good. But what if section=null and env=0? Returns disabled config instead of null — `attachSpillWiring` checks `spills != null && spills.isActive` → skip. Same outcome. OK.

10. The `buildPreview` early-return branch: header says `[spilled: N chars, L lines (threshold T chars)]` — good; body rendered whole; then `$spillReadHint` directly after body without a blank line? Let's compare: covered branch = `'$body\n' '$spillReadHint'` — no blank line between body and hint. Old shape: `'$tail\n' '$spillReadHint'` — also no blank line. Consistent. OK.

11. One more possible edge: `buildPreview` boundary `body.length <= headChars + tailChars` — at exactly head+tail, whole body once. Old behavior at exactly head+tail: head = headChars, tail = tailChars, omitted = 0 → `[... 0 chars omitted ...]` duplicated nothing (head+tail adjacent, no overlap, no negative marker) — so old rendered body once too plus a silly "[... 0 chars omitted ...]" marker. New: no marker. Better.

But hold on — the old code had a REAL bug for bodies in (max(head,tail), head+tail): duplicated overlapping region AND negative omitted count. Was that reachable pre-PR? Only when body.length <= head+tail AND body.length > threshold. Default threshold 8192 > 4000 → unreachable with defaults; reachable with a small configured threshold (e.g. threshold 3000, head/tail 2000 → body 3500: head 2000 + tail 2000 = 4000 > 3500 → duplicated 500 chars + omitted -500). So the bug was reachable pre-PR with custom config; the PR fixes it. Good — no compat concern since legacy default shapes are byte-identical.

arguments.content:
🚨 **BLOCKING: `withCompactionTriggerTokens` throws `ArgumentError` for `FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS=1`**

`base.keepRecentTokens.clamp(1, clamped ~/ 2)` throws in Dart when `lowerLimit > upperLimit`, i.e. whenever `clamped ~/ 2 == 0` — which happens exactly for the parse-valid value `1` (`+1` and `" 1 "` too; the parse only rejects non-integers and `<= 0`).

Reproduced against the packaged API:

```text
Invalid argument(s): 1
dart:core                      int.clamp
.../src/compaction/bench_trigger.dart 59:38  withCompactionTriggerTokens
```

The blast radius is not the function alone: `_effectiveCompactionSettings` feeds every compaction gate — the run-loop auto-compact gate (`agent_cli_compaction.dart:342`), the resumed-session boot cap (`agent_cli_compaction.dart:402`), and the resume parity budget (`session_commands.dart:604`) — all evaluated OUTSIDE try/catch. So this env value doesn't degrade to the default (the way junk does); it kills the whole bench run/boot with an unhandled `ArgumentError`, defeating the file's own "junk never breaks a boot" robustness contract for a one-character typo.

Fix (one line) plus a pinning test:

```dart
final keep = base.keepRecentTokens.clamp(1, max(1, clamped ~/ 2));
```

(or floor the trigger, e.g. treat `clamped < 2` as `keep = 1`).

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: env knob silently rewrites an explicit `config.compactionSettings` override — and the docs disagree about that**

The PR description states: *"Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults **but not over an explicit config override**."* The code says the opposite: `base = override ?? wiring`, then `resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...)` is applied unconditionally — so `FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS` recomputes `reserveTokens`/`keepRecentTokens` **on top of** a user-pinned `compactionSettings` yaml section. The in-code comment ("must win over both the defaults and a host default override") is ambiguous about the explicit-override case, and no test pins either precedence (`agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` builds its config without `compactionSettings`).

Pick one contract and pin it:

- If the description is right (config override wins), skip the knob when `override != null`:

```dart
final base = override ?? resolveCompactionHostWiring(...).settings;
if (override != null) return base; // explicit pin beats the bench env
return resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...);
```

- If the code is right (env wins everywhere), fix the PR description and add a test asserting the composed reserve over an explicit override.

Either way, please also cover the `override.enabled: false` case in the test (that path correctly returns `base` today via the `!base.enabled` guard).

💡 **SUGGESTION: env override drops the section's tolerant-parse notes and prints no override notice**

Two small observability gaps in the composition:

1. When a `spills:` yaml section exists and the env overrides it, the composed `SpillsConfig` discards `base.notes` — so tolerant-parse diagnostics (clamped `headChars`/`tailChars`, unknown keys) that would normally print at boot silently disappear on exactly the bench runs where you're most likely debugging config.
2. The new `attachSpillWiring` note (`[spills] enabled via FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD=…`) prints only when `config.spills == null`; when the env **retunes** an existing section's threshold, nothing says so.

Suggest preserving the notes (`notes: base.notes`) and widening the notice to cover the override case (e.g. `'[spills] threshold overridden via $spillThresholdEnvVar: ${section.threshold} → ${spills.threshold}'`).

💡 **SUGGESTION: a command whose first line is empty renders a faceless label**

`command.indexOf('\n')` runs on the **untrimmed** command, so a multi-line command starting with a newline (`"\nfoo\nbar"`) produces `firstLine == ''` and the label degenerates to `" […7 chars…]"` — leading space, no command face. The multi-line branch checks `command.trim().contains('\n')` but slices the untrimmed original.

Take the first line from the trimmed command:

```dart
final trimmed = command.trim();
final firstLineEnd = trimmed.indexOf('\n');
final firstLine = (firstLineEnd < 0 ? trimmed : trimmed.substring(0, firstLineEnd))
    .replaceAll(RegExp(r'\s+'), ' ')
    .trim();
```

Cosmetic (the label stays bounded either way), but it's a one-line hardening of a brand-new public API.

blocks.text:
All 25 new tests pass. Now let me continue the deep review. Remaining checks:

1. AGENTS.md conventions — check for env-var and export-list conventions.
2. Check `_effectiveCompactionSettings` consistency — the flutter_app parity test (`flutter_app/test/compaction_host_wiring_test.dart`) — does the app path need the bench knob too? The knob is CLI-only (documented). Check parity test still passes (settings semantics unchanged when env unset).
3. Check `resolveRunSpillsConfig` notes-drop wrinkle.
4. Check `benchCompactionTriggerTokens` — `int.tryParse` accepts leading `+`? `int.tryParse('+5')` = 5 in Dart. Fine.
5. Look at the `withCompactionTriggerTokens` doc "Two guards" listing three bullets — nit.
6. Check the interaction: `_effectiveCompactionSettings` with explicit `config.compactionSettings` override — env knob modifies it (contradicts PR description text "wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override"). Check the code comment again: "must win over both the defaults and a host default override". "host default override" = `resolveCompactionHostWiring` default? The PR description says "Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override." But the code applies the bench resolution unconditionally over `base` (which may be the explicit override). So the description is wrong OR the code is wrong. Which is intended? The doc comment in bench_trigger.dart and the code comment say it must win over both. The PR description contradicts. This is a doc/behavior mismatch worth an IMPORTANT or SUGGESTION. Since behavior: env knob overriding an explicit user config — for a bench run, the env is set by the bench harness intentionally; the machine operator sets both. Hmm, precedence question: user config file `compactionSettings` is an explicit user pin; env FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS is set by the bench harness (which is itself the user/automation). The PR description and code disagree — at minimum the description/comment mismatch is confusing. Let me determine the actual intent from tests: `agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` constructs AgentCliConfig WITHOUT compactionSettings, so no test covers env-vs-explicit-override. The code comment says "must win over both the defaults and a host default override" — the PR description says the opposite for explicit config. I'll flag as IMPORTANT (documented contract contradiction; add a test pinning the intended precedence).

Wait, actually let me re-read the PR description: "Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults but not over an explicit config override." And the code: `resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...)` where base = override ?? wiring. Since the bench resolution is applied to `base` regardless, the env knob DOES override the explicit config (when trigger < window - override.reserveTokens). So PR description's "but not over an explicit config override" is FALSE per the code. The code comment says "must win over both the defaults and a host default override" — "a host default override" might mean the host-wiring defaults, not the user's explicit config.compactionSettings. So per the comment, does the knob win over `config.compactionSettings`? The comment is ambiguous. The behavior: yes it wins. The PR description: no it shouldn't. One of them is wrong. Flag it.

7. `agent_cli_spill.dart` — the `io.writeln('[spills] enabled via ...')` prints the raw env value. Value is an integer string; not a secret. OK. But note: it prints only when `config.spills == null` — when the env overrides an existing section's threshold, notice; minor.

8. `resolveRunSpillsConfig` drops section notes when env positive. The notes would have been printed by `attachSpillWiring` — losing them changes diagnostics under env runs. Minor suggestion.

9. `SpillsConfig(enabled: false)` for env `0`: `isActive` false → attach skipped. Good. But what if section=null and env=0? Returns disabled config instead of null — `attachSpillWiring` checks `spills != null && spills.isActive` → skip. Same outcome. OK.

10. The `buildPreview` early-return branch: header says `[spilled: N chars, L lines (threshold T chars)]` — good; body rendered whole; then `$spillReadHint` directly after body without a blank line? Let's compare: covered branch = `'$body\n' '$spillReadHint'` — no blank line between body and hint. Old shape: `'$tail\n' '$spillReadHint'` — also no blank line. Consistent. OK.

11. One more possible edge: `buildPreview` boundary `body.length <= headChars + tailChars` — at exactly head+tail, whole body once. Old behavior at exactly head+tail: head = headChars, tail = tailChars, omitted = 0 → `[... 0 chars omitted ...]` duplicated nothing (head+tail adjacent, no overlap, no negative marker) — so old rendered body once too plus a silly "[... 0 chars omitted ...]" marker. New: no marker. Better.

But hold on — the old code had a REAL bug for bodies in (max(head,tail), head+tail): duplicated overlapping region AND negative omitted count. Was that reachable pre-PR? Only when body.length <= head+tail AND body.length > threshold. Default threshold 8192 > 4000 → unreachable with defaults; reachable with a small configured threshold (e.g. threshold 3000, head/tail 2000 → body 3500: head 2000 + tail 2000 = 4000 > 3500 → duplicated 500 chars + omitted -500). So the bug was reachable pre-PR with custom config; the PR fixes it. Good — no compat concern since legacy default shapes are byte-identical.

12. `_codepointSafeSlice` vs spill's `_headExcerpt`: consistent rules. OK.

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: `withCompactionTriggerTokens` throws `ArgumentError` for `FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS=1`**

`base.keepRecentTokens.clamp(1, clamped ~/ 2)` throws in Dart when `lowerLimit > upperLimit`, i.e. whenever `clamped ~/ 2 == 0` — which happens exactly for the parse-valid value `1` (`+1` and `" 1 "` too; the parse only rejects non-integers and `<= 0`).

Reproduced against the packaged API:

```text
Invalid argument(s): 1
dart:core                      int.clamp
.../src/compaction/bench_trigger.dart 59:38  withCompactionTriggerTokens
```

The blast radius is not the function alone: `_effectiveCompactionSettings` feeds every compaction gate — the run-loop auto-compact gate (`agent_cli_compaction.dart:342`), the resumed-session boot cap (`agent_cli_compaction.dart:402`), and the resume parity budget (`session_commands.dart:604`) — all evaluated OUTSIDE try/catch. So this env value doesn't degrade to the default (the way junk does); it kills the whole bench run/boot with an unhandled `ArgumentError`, defeating the file's own "junk never breaks a boot" robustness contract for a one-character typo.

Fix (one line) plus a pinning test:

```dart
final keep = base.keepRecentTokens.clamp(1, max(1, clamped ~/ 2));
```

(or floor the trigger, e.g. treat `clamped < 2` as `keep = 1`).
"}

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: env knob silently rewrites an explicit `config.compactionSettings` override — and the docs disagree about that**

The PR description states: *"Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults **but not over an explicit config override**."* The code says the opposite: `base = override ?? wiring`, then `resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...)` is applied unconditionally — so `FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS` recomputes `reserveTokens`/`keepRecentTokens` **on top of** a user-pinned `compactionSettings` yaml section. The in-code comment ("must win over both the defaults and a host default override") is ambiguous about the explicit-override case, and no test pins either precedence (`agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` builds its config without `compactionSettings`).

Pick one contract and pin it:

- If the description is right (config override wins), skip the knob when `override != null`:

```dart
final base = override ?? resolveCompactionHostWiring(...).settings;
if (override != null) return base; // explicit pin beats the bench env
return resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...);
```

- If the code is right (env wins everywhere), fix the PR description and add a test asserting the composed reserve over an explicit override.

Either way, please also cover the `override.enabled: false` case in the test (that path correctly returns `base` today via the `!base.enabled` guard).
"}

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md","content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: env override drops the section's tolerant-parse notes and prints no override notice**

Two small observability gaps in the composition:

1. When a `spills:` yaml section exists and the env overrides it, the composed `SpillsConfig` discards `base.notes` — so tolerant-parse diagnostics (clamped `headChars`/`tailChars`, unknown keys) that would normally print at boot silently disappear on exactly the bench runs where you're most likely debugging config.
2. The new `attachSpillWiring` note (`[spills] enabled via FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD=…`) prints only when `config.spills == null`; when the env **retunes** an existing section's threshold, nothing says so.

Suggest preserving the notes (`notes: base.notes`) and widening the notice to cover the override case (e.g. `'[spills] threshold overridden via $spillThresholdEnvVar: ${section.threshold} → ${spills.threshold}'`).
"}

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: `withCompactionTriggerTokens` throws `ArgumentError` for `FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS=1`**

`base.keepRecentTokens.clamp(1, clamped ~/ 2)` throws in Dart when `lowerLimit > upperLimit`, i.e. whenever `clamped ~/ 2 == 0` — which happens exactly for the parse-valid value `1` (`+1` and `" 1 "` too; the parse only rejects non-integers and `<= 0`).

Reproduced against the packaged API:

```text
Invalid argument(s): 1
dart:core                      int.clamp
.../src/compaction/bench_trigger.dart 59:38  withCompactionTriggerTokens
```

The blast radius is not the function alone: `_effectiveCompactionSettings` feeds every compaction gate — the run-loop auto-compact gate (`agent_cli_compaction.dart:342`), the resumed-session boot cap (`agent_cli_compaction.dart:402`), and the resume parity budget (`session_commands.dart:604`) — all evaluated OUTSIDE try/catch. So this env value doesn't degrade to the default (the way junk does); it kills the whole bench run/boot with an unhandled `ArgumentError`, defeating the file's own "junk never breaks a boot" robustness contract for a one-character typo.

Fix (one line) plus a pinning test:

```dart
final keep = base.keepRecentTokens.clamp(1, max(1, clamped ~/ 2));
```

(or floor the trigger, e.g. treat `clamped < 2` as `keep = 1`).
"}

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: env knob silently rewrites an explicit `config.compactionSettings` override — and the docs disagree about that**

The PR description states: *"Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults **but not over an explicit config override**."* The code says the opposite: `base = override ?? wiring`, then `resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...)` is applied unconditionally — so `FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS` recomputes `reserveTokens`/`keepRecentTokens` **on top of** a user-pinned `compactionSettings` yaml section. The in-code comment ("must win over both the defaults and a host default override") is ambiguous about the explicit-override case, and no test pins either precedence (`agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` builds its config without `compactionSettings`).

Pick one contract and pin it:

- If the description is right (config override wins), skip the knob when `override != null`:

```dart
final base = override ?? resolveCompactionHostWiring(...).settings;
if (override != null) return base; // explicit pin beats the bench env
return resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...);
```

- If the code is right (env wins everywhere), fix the PR description and add a test asserting the composed reserve over an explicit override.

Either way, please also cover the `override.enabled: false` case in the test (that path correctly returns `base` today via the `!base.enabled` guard).
"}

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md","content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: env override drops the section's tolerant-parse notes and prints no override notice**

Two small observability gaps in the composition:

1. When a `spills:` yaml section exists and the env overrides it, the composed `SpillsConfig` discards `base.notes` — so tolerant-parse diagnostics (clamped `headChars`/`tailChars`, unknown keys) that would normally print at boot silently disappear on exactly the bench runs where you're most likely debugging config.
2. The new `attachSpillWiring` note (`[spills] enabled via FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD=…`) prints only when `config.spills == null`; when the env **retunes** an existing section's threshold, nothing says so.

Suggest preserving the notes (`notes: base.notes`) and widening the notice to cover the override case (e.g. `'[spills] threshold overridden via $spillThresholdEnvVar: ${section.threshold} → ${spills.threshold}'`).
"}

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: `withCompactionTriggerTokens` throws `ArgumentError` for `FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS=1`**

`base.keepRecentTokens.clamp(1, clamped ~/ 2)` throws in Dart when `lowerLimit > upperLimit`, i.e. whenever `clamped ~/ 2 == 0` — which happens exactly for the parse-valid value `1` (`+1` and `" 1 "` too; the parse only rejects non-integers and `<= 0`).

Reproduced against the packaged API:

```text
Invalid argument(s): 1
dart:core                      int.clamp
.../src/compaction/bench_trigger.dart 59:38  withCompactionTriggerTokens
```

The blast radius is not the function alone: `_effectiveCompactionSettings` feeds every compaction gate — the run-loop auto-compact gate (`agent_cli_compaction.dart:342`), the resumed-session boot cap (`agent_cli_compaction.dart:402`), and the resume parity budget (`session_commands.dart:604`) — all evaluated OUTSIDE try/catch. So this env value doesn't degrade to the default (the way junk does); it kills the whole bench run/boot with an unhandled `ArgumentError`, defeating the file's own "junk never breaks a boot" robustness contract for a one-character typo.

Fix (one line) plus a pinning test:

```dart
final keep = base.keepRecentTokens.clamp(1, max(1, clamped ~/ 2));
```

(or floor the trigger, e.g. treat `clamped < 2` as `keep = 1`).
"}

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","content":"⚠️ **IMPORTANT: env knob silently rewrites an explicit `config.compactionSettings` override — and the docs disagree about that**

The PR description states: *"Applies last in `_effectiveCompactionSettings`, so it wins over defaults **but not over an explicit config override**."* The code says the opposite: `base = override ?? wiring`, then `resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...)` is applied unconditionally — so `FAH_COMPACT_TRIGGER_TOKENS` recomputes `reserveTokens`/`keepRecentTokens` **on top of** a user-pinned `compactionSettings` yaml section. The in-code comment ("must win over both the defaults and a host default override") is ambiguous about the explicit-override case, and no test pins either precedence (`agent_cli_bench_compaction_test.dart` builds its config without `compactionSettings`).

Pick one contract and pin it:

- If the description is right (config override wins), skip the knob when `override != null`:

```dart
final base = override ?? resolveCompactionHostWiring(...).settings;
if (override != null) return base; // explicit pin beats the bench env
return resolveBenchCompactionSettings(base, ...);
```

- If the code is right (env wins everywhere), fix the PR description and add a test asserting the composed reserve over an explicit override.

Either way, please also cover the `override.enabled: false` case in the test (that path correctly returns `base` today via the `!base.enabled` guard).
"}

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md","content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: env override drops the section's tolerant-parse notes and prints no override notice**

Two small observability gaps in the composition:

1. When a `spills:` yaml section exists and the env overrides it, the composed `SpillsConfig` discards `base.notes` — so tolerant-parse diagnostics (clamped `headChars`/`tailChars`, unknown keys) that would normally print at boot silently disappear on exactly the bench runs where you're most likely debugging config.
2. The new `attachSpillWiring` note (`[spills] enabled via FAH_SPILL_THRESHOLD=…`) prints only when `config.spills == null`; when the env **retunes** an existing section's threshold, nothing says so.

Suggest preserving the notes (`notes: base.notes`) and widening the notice to cover the override case (e.g. `'[spills] threshold overridden via $spillThresholdEnvVar: ${section.threshold} → ${spills.threshold}'`).
"}

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md — detailed inline comment files"] O4["Always reference inline comment files via the 'comment' field — do NOT use inline 'body'"] O5["Inline comments MUST use a line number that exists in the PR diff"] O6["If a finding is on unchanged code outside the diff, put it in outputs/pr_review_general.md instead"] O1 --> O2 --> O3 --> O4 --> O5 --> O6 ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD F1["outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief Markdown summary, under 20 lines, bullet-focused"] F2["Required sections: Summary, Key Issues, Next Steps"] F3["outputs/pr_review.json — valid JSON with recommendation, summary, inlineComments, issueCounts"] F4["Each inline comment: path, line, startLine, side, comment, severity (BLOCKING|IMPORTANT|SUGGESTION)"] F5["comment must be a path to a file under outputs/pr_review_comments/.md"] F6["outputs/pr_review_general.md — max 1-2 paragraphs, factual, no essays"] F7["If ci_failures.md present → include each failure as 🚨 BLOCKING (full logs in ci_failures_full.log)"] F8["Keep summary under 2 sentences — put details in inline comment files, not in general text"] F9["Severity classification follows general_guidelines.md:
BLOCKING = must fix · IMPORTANT = should fix · SUGGESTION = optional"] F10["Ticket context: verify PR changes satisfy ticket ACs — note gaps in review"] F11["Inline comments MUST target a line that appears in the PR diff
If the line is not in the diff, the comment becomes a general PR comment instead of a review thread"] F12["Use line numbers from the right-hand side of diff hunks
If pr_diff.txt is truncated, run git diff origin/{base}...HEAD to see the full diff"] ``` Example PR review outputs — keep concise: ### outputs/pr_review.json ```json { "recommendation": "BLOCK", "summary": "SQL injection in UserService.js must be fixed before merge.", "generalComment": "outputs/pr_review_general.md", "inlineComments": [ {"path":"src/auth/UserService.js","line":45,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","severity":"BLOCKING"}, {"path":"src/auth/LoginController.js","line":78,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","severity":"IMPORTANT"}, {"path":"src/utils/validation.js","line":23,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md","severity":"SUGGESTION"} ], "issueCounts": {"blocking":1,"important":1,"suggestions":1} } ``` ### outputs/pr_review_general.md ```markdown ## Automated Code Review — BLOCK **Summary**: SQL injection blocks merge. One important issue (weak password validation) and one suggestion (extract duplicated validation). **Next Steps**: 1. Fix SQL injection in UserService.js — use parameterized queries 2. Strengthen password validation (8+ chars, mixed case, numbers, symbols) 3. Extract shared email validation utility ``` ### outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md ```markdown 🚨 **BLOCKING: SQL Injection** User input is interpolated directly into the query at `UserService.js:45`: ```javascript const query = `SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = '${email}'`; ``` Use parameterized queries instead: ```javascript const query = 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?'; await db.query(query, [email]); ``` ``` # Review verdict rules — machine protocol (binding) The review↔rework loop is a machine, not a conversation: your `recommendation` in `outputs/pr_review.json` is parsed mechanically and drives issue labels, rework runs and CI (each wasted round costs 15–20 CI minutes — gh-71). These rules govern the verdict; every other instruction (severity definitions, output files, thread etiquette) is unchanged. ## Verdict mapping Classify findings exactly as instructed: - 🚨 **BLOCKING** — correctness/bug findings: broken behavior, failing gates (red CI), scope violations, security issues, data loss. - ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability debt worth fixing, but the PR works as shipped. - 💡 **SUGGESTION** — style, wording, import order, dartdoc refs, polish. Then map to the verdict: | Findings | `recommendation` | |---|---| | Any 🚨 BLOCKING (correctness/bug) | `REQUEST_CHANGES` — or `BLOCK` for security / data loss | | No 🚨 BLOCKING — only ⚠️ / 💡 remain | `APPROVE` | `APPROVE` with remaining ⚠️/💡 findings is the expected terminal state (`allowApproveWithSuggestions: true`): post every remaining finding as before (inline threads + general comment) — they do **not** block the merge and must **not** trigger another rework round. ## Anti-patterns (observed live, gh-71) - ❌ Returning `REQUEST_CHANGES` because a re-review surfaced new suggestion-level nits (docs wording, import style, dartdoc refs). A cycle with only suggestion-level findings **must** converge to `APPROVE`. - ❌ `REQUEST_CHANGES` while `issueCounts.blocking` is `0` — the machine treats that as an approval and skips the rework round. Keep `issueCounts` accurate: it is the machine's source of truth, not prose. The machine also cross-checks the counter against your inline comments (a `severity: "BLOCKING"` entry or a 🚨 marker in the referenced comment file) before honoring a blocking-0 approval — if any finding is truly blocking, set `recommendation: REQUEST_CHANGES` with `blocking: 1`+. - ❌ Verdict-by-prose: never phrase the verdict only in the summary text.
